wine: Cascina degli Ulivi Ivag Gavi Bianco 2021
notes: After consistently running afoul of the Gavi DOCG for his raw and unadorned expressions of Cortese, in 2015 Stefano withdrew this wine from the classification, instead choosing to label it as Ivag (Gavi backwards), an indication of his thoughts on the consorzio's conventionally-leaning stipulations. Pulled from 3 parcels of Cortese spread throughout the property and aged for a year in large botti, the Ivag is golden, fleshy, electric and raw: salted meyer lemon, citrus oil, sea salt, little white blossoms. In other words, this is Gavi in all its unadorned and punch-drunk glory.

Named in homage to Stefano's beloved Maremma sheep dog, the Filagnotti Bianco is one of a few truly mesmerizing, single-vineyard expressions of Cortese from the estate, pulled from a parcel of 60 year old vines overlooking the nearby village of Tassarolo. Aged for a few brief months in acacia barrels, the Filagnotti displays the mesmerizing density possible when working with old-vine fruit. What feels like gamma rays compressed into liquid form, the Filagnotti takes everything the Ivag does well and does it even better. Sunshine drenched citrus orchard, retro English cider, green melon, and cr

Cortese sourced from one of the highest points in all of the Gavi region, the Montemarino leans into the more savory and spice laden side of Cortese. Pulled from another parcel of 60+ year old vines, subjected to 3 days of skin maceration and aged in large acacia botti, the Montemarino offers something more fleshy and textural than its siblings. A wine that only seems to fully reveal itself after an hour or so of aeration, a patient consumer is lead down a path of golden bosc pear, kumquat, and damson plum with tight lines and a salty bristle discecting throughout.

wine: Cascina degli Ulivi Le Mat du Raisin Rosso 2021
notes: A wicked blend of equal parts Barbera and Dolcetto from prized 60-year-old vines. The grapes in this blend are usually used for two of the estate's top red labels but in vintages not up to par are reclassified into this dynamic, crunchy red. This wine matures for 1 year on its lees in oak barrels and is bottled unfined and unfiltered. Fresh blackberries, raisiny plums, and tart cherries form the backbone of fruit, as moderate tannins underpin mild acidity through a very dry finish. The Bellotti reds always smack of the earth, with dark chocolate and herbs countering the soft, sour-juicy fruit.

Having fostered a culture of polyculturalism and biodynamic farming practices since taking charge of his family’s vines in 1985, Stefano set about focusing his energies on the revival of ‘true’ Cortese wines, though he continued to foster a small parcel of pre-phylloxera Dolcetto vines that remained. You'd be forgiven in thinking while consuming the ‘Nibio’ that you were staring deep into a glass old Nebbiolo here; uncompromising and meditative, the Nibio is 100% Dolcetto - drawn from the same vines mentioned above. 70% Carricante, 30% Catarratto, the ripping Etna Bianco from Graci is loaded with pithy citrus and chiseled yellow stone fruits. Don't get me wrong, the incisive mineral delivery is very much there, front and center though Alberto's interpretation offers more in terms of mouthfeel and texture than most of his peers, lacing notes of white peach, honey and anise into a wine that punches well above its weight.

Drawn from a jigsaw puzzle of tiny parcels strewn across the property, the Maggiorina is dominated by Nebbiolo (40%), Croatina (40%) and Vespolina (5%) but contains upwards of another 9 varietals, both white and red. Lithe, floral and achingly bright, the estate's everyday offering captures the essence of Alto Piemonte - sweet red cherry, crushed alpine flowers, mint and pine. Well worth rotating into your 'everyday' drinker line up

Marco’s Cesanese is a testament to the heights a terroir-driven take on the grape can reach – the Roman red par excellence, it’s often treated just as fodder for trattoria plonk. From marine-sediment rich and volcanic soils, the ‘Veniero’ is lighter in color, has a pronounced mineral-driven backbone, and much less density than usual. As such, this wine is refined and pretty darn gorgeous, a pure pleasure to drink. All de-stemmed Pinot Noir that sees a brief maceration on skins after pressing and spontaneous fermentation in stainless steel; a little frozen must is added in the Spring to induce secondary fermentation in bottle with no added sulfur or disgorgement at any point. Clean and pristine with fresh, flinty minerality alongside wild berries, tart cranberry and plum skin, cold raspberry-mint tea, river stones, and a touch of earth.

Brand new from the estate, Freisa is a cousin to Nebbiolo and can be made in a brighter, berry-laden style (the name comes from the Latin for strawberry ), or turn to darker, deeper tones and show off the serious structure that is certainly a family trait. This is definitely the latter. The nose shows characteristic notes of roses, raspberries, wild strawberries, with an added rush sage, mint, and graphite. Ripe tannins fill the mouth and sweep across the palate, enticing one to go back to the glass almost a little too quickly...

The 2019 Barolo classico is dark, ample, and super expressive, showing juicy and perfectly ripe red fruits, with succulent dark cherry, plum, leather, rose petal and spice, all nicely amplified. Fabulously silky and rounded tannins allows this mid-weight wine to offer plenty to the impatient early consumer (we won’t judge!) with fine balance and all the elements just so well put together. As is often the case, the straight Barolo punches above its weight. Vineyard sites are a stellar collection of parcels from Rocche dell'Annunziata, Boiolo, Sarmassa, Vignane, Codana and a touch of Cannubi.

The Cannubi vineyard is one of the first sites in Barolo to ripen, and the wines tend to show enormous elegance and Nebbiolo fruit purity. The 2018 is bright and effusive, as wines from this cru tend to be; the Rinaldis' offers fine depth and tons of site characters, both of which were hard to achieve in this vintage. Crushed flowers, spice, new leather and macerated cherry are some of the aromatic notes that soar from the glass.

The Cannubi vineyard is one of the first sites in Barolo to ripen, and the wines tend to show enormous elegance and Nebbiolo fruit purity. The 2016 shows all the raciness of this site and power of the vintage to great effect, crushed flowers, mint, spice and red berry fruit filling out the layers of this pliant, silky Barolo. A wine of pure pleasure.

Onto the lighter side of things, here, Grignolino – the ultimate Piemontese 'chillable red' – gets the serious Rinaldi treatment while still maintaining the variety's innate levity. Crushed flowers, spice, and sweet, red-toned fruit are all nicely lifted, with added elemetns of singed orange rind, Angostura bitters and menthol. The palate is fine, fresh, light and taut with a cool finish that binds everything into perfect harmony. Served with a light chill, this will make for a serious warm weather red.

aromas: Lavender, White Pepper, Tobacco, Cedar, Fennel
notes: A rich, heady wine that really captures the essence of the house style, pulled from a more recently planted parcel within the Barolo zone. Immediately you get the sense that this isn't your run-of-the-mill Langhe Nebbiolo. Layers of dark red fruit, lavender, white pepper, and spice reel from the glass. On the palate, plump but tart cherry gives way to sweet, earthy tobacco, cedar and a spritz of fennel seed. It's fresh and vivacious, rocking a medium weight that is at once tight and shapely, giving it that 'baby Barolo' feel. Ripping stuff.

Composed entirely of Sangiovese raised in oak for 12 months, it is floral with a perfume of ripe red cherry, fresh rose petal, and well-integrated oak spices of vanilla and cinnamon. Medium-bodied, with fine tannins and an angular edge of acidity, the palate is quaffable and forward with orange citrus, dusty earth, and dried herbs.

All direct-press Sangio from the heart of Chianti, this mixes bright red fruit with zesty acidity – think pink grapefruit, pomegranate, and cranberry. A nod to owners Jacopo and Mary's tiny pup Elliot (peep the paw prints on the label), this sneaky little number tastes just like summer: strawberries and juicy melon, absolutely refreshing and cleansing.

wine: Caparsa a Doccio Matteo Chianti Classico Riserva 2016

Grapes for ‘Doccio a Matteo’ are manually harvested, with spontaneous fermentation in concrete vats; maturation is in old oak vats for two and a half years. From the stellar, and long-lived 2016 vintage, this is a wine of power, depth, and concentration, with a quixotic sense of exoticness to it. This bottle is likely the greatest beacon of Lambrusco potential this side of the river Po; 100% Lambrusco Ruberti with a nose of grape soda, black-berried fruits, dark chocolate, cocoa and BBQ char. wine: Mazzoni Colline Novaresi Vespolina Il Ricetto 2022
notes: From the Ghemme region of Alto Piemonte, a relatively unsung grape that's a touch of Fleurie, a pinch of Pelaverga, plenty of woodsy, red berry fruit, and a whole lot of fun. Vibrant and easy-drinking, 'Il Ricetto' doles out tart red cherry, wild strawberry, and white pepper alongside brisk acidity and lithe tannins.

Just like Dante and Helena themselves, this wine exudes a welcoming wisdom, with gentle, expressive depth, and a seriousness about its sense of place and handling but never really about itself. Comprised of 80% Sangiovese from the couple's oldest vines, along with Colorino, Malvasia Nera, and Canaiolo, grapes see wild fermentation in concrete with a long maceration, and the wine spends 36 months in Slavonian oak. Bottled without any additions. Opening on the herbal side with a touch of brett, it segues into tart cherry, blue berry, red flowers, and dried apricot, alongside spicy notes of peppe

An out of the ordinary and thus limited release, 'Area 51' is a 50/50 blend of Vigna Vecchia Sangiovese (which sees just a soft pressing) and Trebbiano (which gets 4 months of on-skin maceration.) We're thinking of it as big nod to the days when Sangio was always blended with white varieties; here, aromas and flavors ping pong from red to white and back in a 'best of' manner: candied strawberry, pulply yellow fruit, blood orange, earthy chamomile, and lots of cherries and dried flowers. With super bright, lip-smakcing acidity, lingering, powdery tannins, and a lightly bitter, terracotta finish

In addition to their Tuscan reds, Dante and Helena produce tiny quantities of white wine from older vine Trebbiano and Malvasia. Their 2021 Bianco comprises 50% Trebbiano and 50% Malvasia grown in soils rich in marine fossils; after natural fermentation, it spends four months on the skins, imparting a gorgeous complex of fleshy-fruity, salty, and tannic tones to the final product. With white floral notes, burnt citrus, melon, dried apricot, and sun-baked herbs, great texture, and a mineral-saline finish that goes on and on. Grab a big bottle and dream of spring!

A radiant expression of the Falanghina grape, born from the sun-kissed vineyards of Roccamonfina in Campania, this shows the volcanic soils of Caserta imbuing its distinct mineral presence. ‘Aorivola,’ meaning "golden hour," pays homage to the magical moments when the sun bathes the vineyards, imparting its essence to the grapes. Fermented with wild yeast, then macerated in oak barrels for a short period of time and aged in stainless steel, its pale straw color with golden reflections evokes the warmth of the Mediterranean sun. The Ronc dai Luchis winery is located in Faedis, a town northeast of Udine at the base of the eastern hills of Friuli. It is a small, family business and the Refosco di Faedis vines (also known as Refosco Nostrano) are approximately 80 years old. Refosco is a variety know for its high acidity, but which two years in oak casks has greatly helped tamed here, rounding out to maintain lift and vibrancy. Medium-bodied, tart and tangy but smooth, with violets, rose hips, and berries, with a woodsy/smokey undertone.

Marco Pecorari's San Lurins estate – the name of their region, San Lorenzo Isontino, in local dialect – produces only two wines: a traditional-method sparkling Malvasia Istriana from the family’s 50-year-old vineyards, and this pet-nat style Ribolla Gialla from their only new planting. A lightly sparkling wine with a salty and mineral profile – one that perfectly recalls the surprisingly nearby Adriatic Sea – coupled with Ribolla Gialla hallmark citrus and thyme notes. Crisp, clean, and dry – the ultimate aperitif!

While decidedly old-world in technique and utterly classic for the region – it doesn’t get much more Friuli than Friuliano – there’s nothing staid about Visintini’s ‘Anfora’ offering. It’s a wine that feels surprisingly modern (especially given the estate’s century-plus history) but also somehow ingrained; varietally correct and expressive but with a little added oomph. 100% hand-harvested Friulano macerates for about 38 days in terracotta amphora (Georgian qvevri ) – imparting, in the end, a luscious golden hue and texture to the wine, versus anything tannic or astringent (or particularly ‘or

Claudio's entry level offering delivers insane QPR year in and year out. From 18-year-old vines, a brief 10 days of fermentation and maceration on the skins is followed by aging for 6 months in stainless steel (keeping fruit fresh) and 6 months in Slavonian oak casks (rounding out any harsher angles) prior to bottling. This hits all the Nebbiolo high-note: crushed rose petals, licorice, red berries, orange peel, spice and hints of warm terracotta, all decidedly lithe and airy in tone but never without purpose. This wonderfully vibrant wine is a blend of Trebbiano, Malvasia Toscana, and Ansonica from young vines in Bolsena that spent just three days on the skins before nine months in vats. These were the first grapes Trish harvested last year and the result is a delicate, light and perfumed wine that is a vivid gold in the glass. Weighing in at just eleven degrees of alcohol and with gentle notes of apricot, minerals, and spice it really quenches a thirst.

There is a nimble balance between the dark, meaty fruit indicative of the grape, and the brightness and levity that comes from DeConcilis’ approach to winemaking. A nose of dark plum, blackberry, soy sauce and sweet spices are focused by a harmonious acidity that provides noteworthy clarity and cut to palate that treads a similar profile to the nose. A dusty, mineral edge and supreme aromatic lift lend the Donnaluna an air of something well behind its humble price tag.

Buondonno's Chianti Classico is made from 100% Sangiovese, and is the winery's main wine. The wine is macerated for 20 days in steel and cement with daily reassembly. Aging takes place for 12 months in partially used wooden barrels of different sizes. Juicy, intense, and aromatic, offering the perfect intersection of fleshy cherried fruit, 'eau-de-Italian deli' (espresso, oregano, salumi) and savory, mineral-driven earth.

A blend of Nebbiolo and Freisa, vinified exactly the same as Gianliugi's Barbaresco, this weeknight wonder boasts a harmony of ripe raspberries, cherry and plum fruit and wafts of violets. It’s plush exuberance tempered only by subtle aromas of earth, char and dried leaves. Fresh acidity and a framework of savory tannins means this is destined for the dinner table. Gianluigi Lano is an understated, stoic man who works a small certified organic farmstead in San Rocco Seno d’Elvio, Barbaresco. Old-school Prosecco right here, fermented in bottle with its spent yeast left in place ( col fondo = sur lie ), lending texture, warmth, and just a hint of cloudiness to this very pretty bottle of extra brut bubbles. Floral hints of acacia and rose linger alongside tart citrus, green apple, and white peach. A bright, acid-driven finish cements the 'Credamora' as the ultimate aperitif pairing.

wine: Champagne Egly Ouriet Grand Cru Extra Brut NV

The grapes are grown in a dramatic amphitheater-like plot in the unique and traditional Maggiorina style and completely harvested by hand. After a native yeast fermentation in open-top stainless steel vats (outdoors!), the grapes then macerate for one month. Next, they are pressed and racked to 500 liter oak barrels for a year of elevage

Named in reference to the hillside on which its vines grow, Croci’s Campedello Frizzante sees a blend dominated by Malvasia di Candia Aromatica, with smaller portions of Trebbiano and Ortrugo as well as some splashes of Marsanne and Sauvignon. The fruit here is destemmed and left to ferment spontaneously in vat, with about 2 weeks of maceration on skins before pressing, drawing a deeply golden hue and a touch of additional grip into the wine’s core. Buoyant, joyful, exuberant… hell, we’ll spare you the hyperbole and just let you crack this bottle for yourself! Reeling with a heady melange of t

Old-school Prosecco right here, fermented in bottle with its spent yeast left in place ( col fondo = sur lie ), lending texture, warmth, and a gentle cloudiness to this very pretty bottle of extra brut bubbles. Floral hints of acacia and rose linger alongside tart citrus, green apple, and white peach.

The Padovani sisters of Fonterenza have around 4.2 contiguous hectares in the hills near Poggio San Polo, the southeastern part of the Montalcino zone. Their farming is certified biodynamic, the work painstakingly manual; harvest is always by hand. Their Brunello comes from a mere hectare's worth of fruit from their prized 'Vigna del Bosco' parcel, a site they planted themselves in 2000. (It's is surrounded entirely by the woods, or 'bosco.') Their Brunello spends six years in a 2500L botte and is a concentrated, complex wine: riserva-level in character and beyond riserva in its aging process.

aromas: Pear, Quince, Apricot, Pineapple, Chamomile, Honey
notes: The Gialla Bianco from Colleformica sees us strolling into the very early stages of the ‘orange’ wine spectrum. Crafted with 75% Malvasia di Candia Aromatica and 25% Trebbiano Toscana, the wine sees a 7-day stint macerating on skins before being pressed into fiberglass until bottling the following spring. More aromatically demure than some expressions of Malvasia di Candia we’ve offered in the past, and with a tell-tale and incredibly welcome dollop of balancing salty/savory from the addition of the Trebbiano, the nose here is all baked Asian pear, yellow apple, clover honey, sun-baked golden

wine: Chiara Condello Emilia Sangiovese Riserva Lucciole 2019
notes: Sourced from a tiny parcel of old Sangiovese wines within Chiara’s property, the Le Lucciole Riserva leaves an extraordinarily elegant and refined impression for a region so commonly associated with serviceable yet simplistic wines. Here you’ll find a remarkably fresh and cool-toned expression of Sangio, displaying dusty ripe cherry, smoke and sweet red florals, grounded by a hint of animal muskiness. On the palate, textures of pure silk release tart cherries brought to life by vibrant acidity, as saline-minerals saturate the palate and hints of fine tannin add balance. The finish is long, dis

Vittorio makes minuscule amounts of this rustic, still red wine, a collection of Lambrusco, Malbo Gentile, and those ever-present mystery grapes, hand harvested, destemmed, and fermented dry in fiberglass containers before getting racked to old barrels for aging. ‘Sassoscuro’ is packed with red plum, strawberry, kirsch, blackberry, and other fruits-of-the-forest but has a wonderfully leafy, savory undertone of dark, fresh forest floor, supported by moderate tannins and a mineral-rich earthiness. Easy but intriguing drinking.

Not made every vintage, Vittorio’s ‘Smilzo’ is a beguiling bottle – charming, sophisticated, just a little raffish, and an electric shade of fuchsia in the glass. His signature blend of Lambrusco, Malbo Gentile, and other grapes that shall remain unknown, this sees the same treatment as his other sparklers. A rosato that reads more like a light red, it’s full of tart cranberry, raspberry compote, and sweet herbs, with tiny tongue-pricking bubbles. A surprisingly iron-tinged note and beautiful iced tea-like tannins finish things off on the savory side, but will leave your mouth watering through

'Ripa di Sopravento' is crafted from two hyper-local sub-clone of Trebbiano (plus three ‘mystery grapes’ interplanted amongst them), grapes are de-stemmed, followed by a direct press. The wine ferments in fiberglass containers and after a racking off the lees with 10g of residual sugar left in the must, the wine is bottled, where it then re-ferments to create its crisp, creamy bubbles. An aromatic delight, its punchy nose of apricot tea, quince jam, and Meyer lemon is wound together on a complex and beguiling palate pocked with pulpy yellow fruit, savory rosemary and sweet sage, and crisp mine

One of the most sought-after Lambruscos we carry – yes, it's amazing, but mainly because Vittorio only sends over a shipment every 2 or 3 years! This is very much a 'by hand' operation, from farming to cellar work to Vittorio hand-labeling each bottle, so we can't fault him but consider yourself in the know now. Crafted from a blend of Lambrusco Grasparossa, Malbo Gentile, and some unnamed local grapes, fruit is hand-harvested, destemmed, before undergoing a single fermentation that begins in the tank and ends in the bottle: bottled in the cold months when fermentation stops, in spring with hi

wine: Armato Sciappa Olio d'Oliva Extra Vergine 500ml

The paste that is crafted from the meat of the olive is then deposited onto a handmade rope disc that rotates as the paste piles higher and higher. Tags: after dinner, dessert, dessert wine, lipari, Malvasia delle Lipari, Sicilia, Sicily, Sweet

A 50/50 blend of Sangiovese and Gamay del Trasimeno (the confusingly-named local version of Grenache — no relation to Beaujolais except maybe a glou-glou attitude!) Spontaneous fermentation, 6 days skin maceration, then aged in fiberglass tanks; like all wines in the lineup, no added sulfur and no filtering or fining. This red is the first to be released — medium-bodied, uplifting, gentle tannins, a spicy nose (with a little bit of funk to blow off), silky red fruits, and a cab franc-like savoriness. A surprisingly fresh, down-to-earth explosion of berries, cassis and pomegranate, full of ener

100% Trebbiano d’Abruzzo with 8 days of skin contact; aged in fiberglass. Like a generator in a bottle, this light, bright orange wine keeps on giving. On the nose, cara cara orange juice and white flowers; on the palate, it’s vibrant and zesty, with notes of passion fruit, hibiscus, orange rind, and almonds, great acidity and a dry finish. Will quench the thirst of any skin-contact aficionado while also convincing the uninitiated to jump on board the orange bandwagon.

Camilla Rossi Chauvenet is making modern, enegetic wines in a fairly stodgy region; she was the first in Valpolicella to make sparkling wine with Corvina in this 'sur lie' style -- born from a challenge to make the minerality and freshness of her grapes the star of the show, but also because she loves pet-nat. Italians know that the spent lees at the bottom of a non-disgorged bottle are the good bits, adding depth of flavor (Camilla encourages you to (rotate this unfiltered wine several times in the bottle to enhance the experience of this elegant natural wine') and in this case pairing perfec

Enzo’s Primatraccia Bianco feels like a day at the beach in liquid format: a refreshing dunk in an ocean of briney, sun-drenched, and smile inducing grape juice. 100% Trebbiano grown along Enzo’s calcareous hillsides, the wine undergoes spontaneous fermentations in steel tanks with a few days macerating on skins before being transferred to clay amphora (as seen on the label) for 6-8 months of development, bottled without any filtration of sulphur. More sunny-hued than truly orange in appearance, the Primatraccia moves past some initial funk to reveal oodles of pickley yellow citrus zest, salte

Mocha, tobacco and spice aromas lead the way, while the ripe, open palate offers baked plum, espresso and coconut alongside close-grained tannins. While winemaker Patrizia Cencioni’s family roots reach back decades in Montalcino, this is not your typical tale of wine-stained generations, each planting vines and learning from the next. Patrizia wanted to make Brunello wines; thus, she bought a crumbling property on the southeast flanks of Montalcino in 1989—not far from the lauded Casanova di Neri—and set to doing things her way. Thirty years later, the estate is a shining example of how hard w

A head-turning and joy-inducing turn on the Sangiovese grape. Non-existent are the dusty tannins and more brooding fruit often associated with traditional renditions of the grape; instead this is a gentle and sexy beast - wrapped in a powdery soft, velvet texture we find oodles of ripe and candied cherry and raspberry fruit projected through a prism of high-toned dried rose petal aromatics. Fermented and aged in fiberglass with the slightest dash of SO2. Serve ever so slightly chilled.

wine: Gianni Brunelli Le Chiuse  di Sotto Brunello di Montalcino 2018
notes: The 2018 Brunello di Montalcino does a great job of capturing the essence and the spirit of Sangiovese, a grape that delivers infinitely nuanced and complex results when in the right hands. Mint, lavender and fennel lead on the nose, while sweet, juicy persimmon and crisp pomegranate provide the backdrop on the palate. The youthful density of the ripe primary fruit contrasts with salty minerality and lively acidity, leaving a cascading and crisp impression on the palate. As with the 2017 vintage, Laura Brunelli will not be releasing a Riserva. Instead, the Olmo vineyard, which typically forms

Siro's Sassella reveals another, darker-noted level of fruit and spice on the palate, with five-spice and brambly berries, tart red currant, caramelized sugar, and bresaola, wrapped around an inner, red floral sweetness. Fine, pin-prick-like tannins continue this dynamic, creating an interplay between luscious and pleasingly bitter/drying, leading to a lip-smacking, savory finish. A Nebbiolo that displays Burgundian richness and elegance and the lacy finesse of much bigger name Piemontese producers, this one's ready to go between now and the next 5 years.

Born from a trip to Alsace, where Corrado was inspired by the idea of expressing terroir and season not through a single variety wine but by mixing different grapes from the same soil, the 'Metccio' also nods to the traditions of the Marche; until the mid-90s, mixing different grapes from a vineyard site was the norm, vinifying by single varietal only a very recent phenomena born from enology and marketing. A co-fermentation of white grapes and red grapes spontaneously fermented, Corrado knocked this one out of the park – a joyful, moreish melange marked by red berries, touches of tropical ton

A blend of Trebbiano, Malvasia and Verdicchio from three parcels of vines young and old. The grapes were fermented on the skins for three weeks before being pressed off to concrete vats for a year of rest. A vibrant, sunshiny shade of amber, this is heady with ripe citrus, earth and spice, while tea-like tannins frame flavors of apricot, minerals and bitter herbs.

Sourced from two plots of Verdicchio that both lie within the borders of the classic Castelli di Jesi growing zone - one up in the mountains, the other neighboring the cantina - the Terre Silvate is fermented and aged in old concrete vats and while the majority is given a direct press, around twenty percent sits on skins for a few days, lending a little flesh and grip. Open and expressive in its youth, it pairs stone fruits, brine and a pleasant, almond-like bitterness to great effect.

From the singular contrada of Crasà, the 2018 Rosso 'Alberello' hails from a parcel of century-old (plus!), pre-phylloxera vines planted in the ancient bush vine (i.e. alberello) format. This corner of Etna is home to softer, more ashen volcanic soils, the resulting wines offering an extreme aromatic punch as a result. Intensely floral and perfumed, the wine reels with dried rose, powdered cocoa, dark cherry skin and raspberry candies straddled across a palate that is at once precise, complex, rich, lithe, persistent... we could go on and on.

wine: Lodi Corazza Colli Bolognesi Venti Pignoletto Frizzante 2018
notes: Obtained from an extraordinary local grape of Romagna - Pignoletto, more commonly known as Grechetto Gentile. This Pignoletto Frizzante is the typical wine of Bologna: easy-to-drink with delicious fruity aroma combined with fine bubbles, making it perfect as an aperitif or for the classic local cuisine. It is made with hand-harvested Pignoletto grapes, which then go through the Martinotti method - meaning secondary fermentation in stainless steel tanks - in order to refine its bubbles. The final wine has elegant notes of stone fruit and soft mineral edges.

wine: LeLarge Pugeot Tradition Brut Nature NV
notes: The family's entry-level stunner features a Meunier-dominant blend that spotlights the drive and poise of the estate’s leading lady, the underappreciated Pinot Meunier grape. This bottling is the platonic ideal of growers’ champagne - seeming to seamlessly weave the high-toned mineral streak of Vrigny with the delicate and more savory leaning aromas of this red grape-dominant blend, drawn from a total of 30 parcels within Vrigny. 50% Meunier, 40% Pinot Noir, 10% Chardonnay. wine: Lassaigne Le Cotet Blanc de Blancs Extra Brut NV
notes: From the chalkiest parcel of Lassaigne’s vineyard in Montgueux, Le Cotet delivers on that minerality in its seashell-like notes and salt-air acidity. It’s a powerful chardonnay Champagne, the chalkiness mellowed with flavors of fresh almonds, scents of dried flowers and gingerbread spice. Like all of Lassaigne’s wines, it’s made without added yeast and with only a slight addition of sulfur at the press (none after).

We're #blessed to have snagged one of the few 6-packs of this juicy, large-format slugger to have made it to the west coast. 2 liters (yes, 2 whole liters) of bright and easy Veneto sunshine in a big ol' bottle, the Vino da Tavola is a laid back amalgamation of Merlot, Refosco, Cab Franc and Raboso, perfectly primed as the ultimate party favor. Unabashedly easy going and fresh, this will make for a killer bottle to share with friends al fresco.

A 10 day maceration on skins lends the '450' a deeply golden hue and more textural weight than its compatriots. With first fermentation in steel, second fermentation in bottle - basically an un-disgorged Champagne for orange wine aficionados.From vines planted in the early 1950s, the 450 leans heavily into the citrus skin/oil side of things capturing zesty pink grapefruit, Cara Cara orange and tangerine in a web of dusty stone and white orchid. L ow in alcohol but the most structured of their wines, though never sacrificing a hallmark saline freshness.

The story of Le Sincette lies right in the producer’s colorful labels. Splashes of purple for grapes, green for olive groves, a big dollop of blue denoting the nearby shores of Lake Garda, along with drawings of the plants and animals that grow there alongside the vines. Having purchased the property in the late 1970s, the Brunori family have spent the last 4 decades bringing light to some of Lombardia’s lesser known vinous stars such as Marzemino, Rebo, and, most importantly for them, Groppello. The Brunoris have taken their stewardship of this place to extreme lengths; not only were they one

wine: Podere Veneri Vecchio BellaCiao Agostinella Bianco 2020
notes: Raffaello Annichiarico has been producing in the province of Benevento since 1999. His wines have a very precise idea at their base: to create an ecosystem in synergy between man and nature. A deeply amber wine, with lots of white flowers, citrus and pulpy fruit notes, mineral, herbaceous overtones and some serious but never astringent tannic bite.

aromas: Raspberry, Espresso, Mushroom, Eucalyptus, Bay Leaf
notes: The year is 2001; after a professional lifetime in front of a computer screen at some of Italy’s most prominent “.com”-era organizations, Bruno Giacometto decided it was a good point in his life to spend a little more of his time… outside. With his aging parents beginning to weary amidst the day-to-day operations of the winery they founded in the mid-1960s, Bruno returned to his birthplace in Piemonte’s rural and remote northwest to take the reins of his family’s estate, stewarding it forward into the 21st century. wine: Poderi Veneri Vecchio Oh Oh Camajo Rosso 2021
notes: Oh Oh! Camajo! from Podere Veneri Vecchio is comprised solely of Campania native Camaiola. Raffaello Annicchiarico, agronomist and former microbiologist, is vigneron and manager of his small estate and cellar located 100-200 meters above sea level in the province of Benevento. The terroir of this region - of volcanic origin and mainly composed of clay-heavy sediments - combined with the typically mild and windy climate of this area, give the wines their unique signature, and Raffaele has been operating organically since day one, in order to best preserve all the typical territorial characteris

An elegant red that is based on 90% Nerello Mascalese and 10% Nerello Cappuccio that mostly come from 80-100 year-old vines in Solicchiata. Almost rosé-like in hue, it is utterly true to a varietal character that is based on delicacy rather than intensity. Thought to be a hybrid of Sangiovese and Mantonico Bianco, it’s not surprising that Nerello Mascalese doesn’t yield a powerhouse of a wine. wine: Mazzoni Colline Novaresi Vespolina Il Ricetto 2020
notes: From the Ghemme region of Alto Piemonte, a relatively unsung grape that's a touch of Fleurie, a pinch of Pelaverga, plenty of woodsy, red berry fruit, and a whole lot of fun. Vibrant and easy-drinking, 'Il Ricetto' doles out tart red cherry, wild strawberry, and white pepper alongside brisk acidity and lithe tannins.

The 'wonder child' in Dario's stable and arguably the benchmark grape of Oslavia, Princic's Ribolla spends 30 days on skins before aging in combination of old acacia and chestnut barrels. Deeply golden and silkily textured, the palate is chock with salty apricot skin, orange liqueur, lemon verbena, rosewater and creme caramel, the fruit stealthily unfolding in the mouth to reveal a wine deceptively supple in body, though there is plenty of underlying backbone by way of acid and fine tannins that promise a long life for this stunner. This will be a great wine to watch over the next decade or co

Dario's spiced and savory 'Jakot' is from 60-year-old Friulano vines - 'Jakot' being the winking, local nomenclature for native Tocai ('Tokaj') Friulano. 22 days of on-skin maceration followed by 24-30 months of aging in Slovenian oak barrels culminate in an amber wine of undeniable richness and outstanding length. Leading with notes of dried fruit and medicinal, mountain herbs on the nose, with time it subtly sheds layers to reveal a more fresh and vibrant side - apricot, lemon confit, yellow plums, mandarin orange, and candied ginger. Bergamot, sage, and toasted bitter almond round out the m

A sulfur-free sparkling rosé from the Gambellara subregion of Veneto. Made from local red grape Corvina with Garganega must, ‘Confondo' is a play on Col Fondo, meaning "on the lees", which give the wine its lovely hazy character. Everything is done by hand in the production here, and the result is fruity and clean, with red currant and apple skin, strawberry and lemon, and a tart and tangy dry finish to cut any sweetness. A no brainer for sunny days!

The Parasiliti's baseline Etna Rosso contains fruit from vines averaging 80 years of age, spread across the contradas of Crasa and Calderara. Dominated by Mascalese with a small percentage of Nerello Cappuccio and Mirello Rossa, fermentation occurs in botte grande before transferring to cement in an effort to retain tension and verve. Tightly wound red berries, red cherry and cherry stone cushion a core of flinty woodsmoke, singed orange and wild herbs, emerging from a palate that is as lengthy as it is pure and juicy.

Warmly integrated with soft black tea-like tannins, black licorice, citrus zest and an almost pottery-like, earthen tone that just feels Sicilian, the Passofonduto is balanced with bright, earthy plum, and a host of savory, mineral aromas and flavors. This wine may emerge in the coming years as one of Sicily's truly great, standard-bearing wines!

This 2016 is only the second edition of this magical but unfortunately rare bottling. This is a complex and meticulous blend of all the house's cuvées in the most difficult years. It is a mix of 80% Chardonnay and 20% Pinot Noir, 100% vinified in used Leflaive barrels. Its fine bubbles release an appealing nose featuring aromas of sweet-ripe citrus fruits, peach and red berries backed with notes of roasted nuts and some baked apple. A very complex palate in the mouth showing citrus spice and profound minerality with a lot of tension as well as great length and grace.

notes: Tight, tart, and wonderfully evocative of northern Italy. The Antoniotti's low-intervention, very clean winemaking has resulted in a fresh young wine redolent of red cherry, rose petal, dusty sandalwood spice, a hint of black pepper, and slightly under-ripe strawberry. Mostly Nebbiolo, with Croatina and Vespolina, just about the same blend as their Bramaterra bottling, but in a more accessible style. Vibrant, pure, and delicate with subtle red apple skin-like tannin. A strong contender for your new house red!

Barolo who? Odilio has forever been a strong believer in the ‘choir’ of additional varieties traditional to Alto Piemonte’s Nebbiolo-based wines; heavy doses of Croatina and Vespolina here lend noticeable purity and concentration, though its lithe frame and firmer angles speak clearly of the wine’s sub-alpine, higher elevation heritage. Spending 36 months in oak, it shows less primary fruit and more darker black cherry liqueur and earth-driven spice. Licorice notes, powdered violet, bergamot, whole black peppercorns, and an almost peaty-like character stand front and center. aromatically. Engl

Some say the tiny wine region of Molise is Italy’s last hidden gem. Tucked away on the southern cusp of the high Apennines, the land here rolls from the steep slopes of interior Abruzzo to the southern plains of Puglia. Wine exports to the US are few and far between, but we managed to score a real gem here! Comprised of 50% Tintilla (a local varietal), 25% Falanghina and 25% Trebbiano Toscano the Tagada is a super sour, tart, and lively red. With fresh acidity and a youthful finish, this chillable, low ABV wine is supremely sluggable with notes of cranberry, kaffir lime, and orange peel.

The Libero sees 12 months in old oak tonneaux. Its freshness and precision galore on offer here, with Sangiovese fruit so defined that it almost feels three dimensional in the mouth: sweet red and black cherry and blackberry hover beneath lifted aromatics of violet and underbrush with a sweetly savory, almost tarry note adding some really meditative complexity.

Offering endless white flowers-lime blossom, daisy, viburnum jasmine-followed by golden apple, basil and lime. Taut, vertical and savory, the Ambaraba is testament to how well bottle-fermented wines develop over the course of a few years, snapping shut with a finish of moreish yellow citrus and rock salt.
A striking rosato made of Barbera. Off-dry and slightly frizzante; think raspberry soda, cherry, and lavender on a raft of subtle bubbles.

Orange peel, apricot, wild sage, and hints of candied fruit abound, carried on intense tannins well balanced by searing acidity. Not for the faint of heart but absolutely delicious when given a little time, air, and an open mind (a hunk of prosciutto wouldn't hurt either).

aromas: Raspberry, Strawberry, Black Cherry, White Pepper, Star Anise
notes: A Nero d'Avola with aromas of strawberry, star anise and raspberry that carry through to the palate alongside notes of white pepper and black cherry jam. Juicy and straightforward, it's made to be enjoyed soon, and tableside.

JYP's Moscato stays 2 weeks on skins before being pressed, leading to a wine that is magnificently aromatic, bone dry with some tannins, full of texture still with great acidity to balance all the banana blossom, star fruit, tangelo, alpine herbs, and humidity. Downright lip-smacking with tension and freshness in spades and perfectly balanced: a very fine mountain Muscat.

A wonderfully fresh, cloudy sparkling wine made with the pretty, perfumed local variety, Malvasia di Candia. Initially fermented in vat, the wine is transferred to bottle with a little must for the second fermentation. The gentle bubbles carry pure, vibrant flavours of grapefruit zest before a clean, salty finish.

The queen of the native varieties of Breganze, named after the hungry wasps (vespe) that target its sweet grapes. Typically Vespaiolo is more widely cultivated as a passito version, known as Torcolato di Breganze. Grown on various plots between the Breganzese hills, the vineyards are from 4 to 20 years old grown on volcanic and clay soil; there is one plot that has a lot of silt which gives the wine a note of freshness. Harvested in early September and fermented in concrete tanks. Vespaiolo is a complex grape that creates dry white wines with minerality and acidity that intertwines with the de

100% Cannonau di Sardegna, the Bobboti is a combination of two parcels: 75% is pulled from a younger vineyard averaging 20-30 years of age, with the remaining portion drawn from the century-old parcel planted nearby. Named in reference to a local ‘Bogeyman’-like figure, the Bobboti is unashamedly fruit forward and decidedly Medditeranean in its warmth; juicy blueberry, strawberry and ripe plum dominate the fruit, intersected by savory lines of scrubby herbs and white pepper. To look at in the glass one assumes something a little less dense and lengthy, yet what emerges is a bombastic mouthful

5ha vineyard near the sea, opposite the Aeolian Islands. The sun, the heat and the cool sea breeze wrap around this wine like a gentle hug. Grapes are grown organically with biodynamic treatments. Tones of violets, red currant, and sun-warmed blueberry, with moderate tannins.

From 50+ year old vineyards, this easy-drinking Dolcetto is full of wild blackberries and almonds, with pleasantly soft tannins and a nicely balanced lighter body. Dolcetto is typically the first grape to ripen and for this reason it is called it “Svicc”, local Piemontese dialect for “awake”.

Equal parts Trebbiano, Malvasia and Bombino aged in stainless and without skin contact; an honest and straightforward nod to the Frascati wines of old, that retains an elegance and precision that transcends first impressions. Golden apples, lemon pith and smoky earth laced with pocks of ginger, geranium and spearmint.

Dominated by the southern Lazio specialty in Cesanese (though Daniele claims it different to the more celebrated clone in nearby Piglio) with smaller percentages of Sangiovese and Montepulciano. Wild blackberry, blackberry leaf and a smidge of balsamic highlight this classically styled red, wrapped neatly in velvety tannins over a mid-weight frame.

100% Montepulciano, with an intense, deep bouquet filled with red fruit, pepper and a whiff of smoke. On the palate it’s medium-bodied, balanced, with crisp acidity, a hint of tannins and a grippy, savory finish. “This wine is produced thanks to the land rich in stones and its exposure, to the sun, to the sea breeze, and to the meticulous work of man.” — Vincezo Di Meo. Comprised entirely of Procanico that sees just under a month on skins maceration in anfora before gentle pressing, followed by aging also in anfora for 5 months, then another 6 months in steel (with some still on skins). 100% Roscetto, a third of which sees 15 days skin maceration and one year of aging in stainless steel on fine lees before bottling. Poggio Bbaranello is the only producer making 100% Roscetto with skin maceration, due to vines being very low yielding. As such, production is super small – less than 300 bottles!

Moscatell D'Alexandria 2024 is a natural wine crafted by La Rural , in the Catalonia region in Spain . Its a floral grape, often used for sweet wines in the conventional wine world, but here in the natural wine scene is often made dry, like this, where to perfumed aromatics really breathe a burst of life to the nose.

Macabeu 2023 is a natural wine crafted by La Rural , in the Catalonia region in Spain . This light 11% white wine with no added sulphites is made with Macabeu grapes, and features a mild smokey reduction, giving it a mystical wild character. Its certainly an adventure, with a little funk too! Otherwise pops of yellow apples, lime, cinnamon, smoke and ash. Pretty cool for those who like things wild!

Cava Rose Brut Nature 2023 is a natural wine crafted by Azimut , in the Catalonia region in Spain . This sparkling wine is made with Grenache , Monastrell and Xarel Lo grapes. Only a small addition of sulphites at bottling is added.

Cava Brut Nature 2023 is a natural wine crafted by Azimut , in the Catalonia region in Spain . This sparkling wine is made with Macabeu , Xarel Lo and Parellada grapes. Expect pops of green apple, bruised pear and soft tropical fruit coming through, with a crisp and energetic perlage that keeps it vibrant, fresh and perky. It's got a little wildness and a little punk rock attitude

Negre 2020 is a natural wine crafted by Azimut , in the Catalonia region in Spain . Expect pops of blackberry, red cherry, and dark forest fruit. Nice acidity, a rustic touch and savoury, Spanish finish that makes it suitable for grilled meats and hearty stews. Aged in concrete tanks and with a little SO2 addition at bottling

Brisat 2023 is a easy going, fresh and vibrant natural wine crafted by Azimut , in the Catalonia region in Spain . Fresh and crisp, offering soft touches of pear, elderflower and peaches with a mild salty touch.

wine: Entre Vinyes - Oniric Gravetat Zero Pet Nat
notes: Oniric Gravetat Zero Pet Nat is a natural wine crafted by Entre Vinyes , in the Catalonia region in Spain . Nicely salty, mineralic and with a pop of pear and lemon sherbert tingling on your palate, this wine is everything a zingy and fresh white pet nat should be!
Rosato is a natural wine crafted by Sette , in the Piedmont region in Italy . 100% Barbera from 15-year-old vines, with a very pale nice colour. We expect good things from this!

Mary of Modena is a natural wine crafted by Il Farneto , in the Emilia-Romagna region in Italy . This sparkling wine is made with a blend of mostly white and but a TOUCH of red grapes too: 60% Spergola, 38% Chardonnay and 2% Termarina grapes (quite a rare one, which is red). We hear this 11.5% fizz to be light and with citrussy undertones, not too fruity with citrus, flowers and cotton candy memories coming through under a nice mineralic edge.

Fresh and uncomplicated classic fun.

Sclopit is a natural wine crafted by Viniverso , in the Friuli Venezia Giulia region in Italy . This red wine is made with 50% Schioppettino and 50% Pinot Noir grapes, and is light at 12.5% but still with Italian soul. Expect bursts of cherry, forest fruits and a little spicey touch

Rossese di Dolceacqua is a natural wine crafted by Antonio Perrino , making wine under the name Testalonga . He is based in the Liguria region in Italy . A challenging grape to master, here Antonio grows 2 hectares of the 80 total on steep vineyard terraces. He also does not add any sulphites in production.

This white wine is made with Moscato di Noto grapes, which is a native Sicilian varietal of Muscat (there are many different ones!). Here there is just a short maceration on the skins, so expect this wine to be more white than orange, as the grape is often made like. Aged in stainless steel tanks for freshness, expect ripe stone fruit, lemon rind and salty aspects too with a mild floral touch.

No added sulphites. Expect depth, tannin, complexity and energy.

Cala Iancu is a natural wine crafted by Il Mortellito , in the south eastern corner of Sicily, in Italy . This white wine is made with Sicilian grapes 90% Grillo and 10% Catarratto grapes, and we hear it is VERY fresh, and very Italian - dolce vita in a glass some would say. Aged in stainless steel tanks to achieve this, we expect this wine to deliver a lot of nice summery vibes and great value too!

Cala Niuru is a natural wine crafted by Il Mortellito , based in the south eastern part of the Sicily, in Italy . This medium-bodied, fresh red wine is made with mostly Frappato and a little Nero d'Avola grapes, which are all grown on Alberello bush vines. This plush and fruity red wine sees 4 days skin contact. Aged in stainless steel tank to maintain freshness, we hear it has notes of cherries, raspberries and a hint of liquorice. Ideal for a weeknight pasta or casual weekend bbq.

Monocromo #1 (Passerina del Frusinata) 2022 is a natural wine crafted by Macciocca , in the Lazio region in Italy . To our knowledge, this wine does not have any added sulphites but this needs verification.

wine: Feral - No. 1 White Szechuan Pepper & Hops

Richly fragrant, with pronounced citrus notes and a tickling spiciness, velvety and spicy.

Homok is one of those wines that is both gluggable on a warm afternoon but also has that zingy, acidic salty bite on the finish - plus it's incredible value!
Brezeme Red MAGNUM by Eric Texier is a natural wine made in Rhone with Syrah grapes.
Cutremur 2021 by Absurde Genies des Fleurs is a natural red wine made in Languedoc with Carignan and Cinsault grapes.

Penumbra 2022 by L'absurde Génie des Fleurs is a natural red wine made in Languedoc with 100% Cinsault grapes, which is 11.5% alcohol and zero added sulphur Expect vibrant acidity and bright fruit with a juicy mouthfeel.
Molinarosa 2021 by Il Roccolo is a natural wine made in Veneto with Garganega grapes. This time not a sparkling. Full of cherries and bright acidity

O’Belix 2021 by Il Roccolo is a natural wine made in Veneto with Molinara grapes. Production details of O'Belix: O'Belix comes from Il Roccolo di Monticelli, a small natural wine project run by Silvia Tezza on the limestone hills between Verona and Soave in Veneto. She farms a recovered old family vineyard using a lunar-calendar approach without synthetic chemistry. The wine ferments naturally and ages in stainless steel before bottling. Tasting Notes: We have not yet tried this vintage of O'Belix by Il Roccolo, but we hear it has notes of pale cherry, dried herbs, almond and a light perfumed

wine: Max Dexheimer - Schmuck Pet Nat Rosé
notes: Max Dexheimer's 'Schmuck Pet Nat' is a natural wine made from Pinot Noir in Rheinhessen, is full of Sour Cherry & Fizzy Sweet notes. Really yummy 10% fizz! Whilst Dexheimer has his Schmuck... there is also the Nice Guy, which is perhaps the opposite and a play on words!
Nice Guy Rosé by Dexheimer is a natural wine made in Rheinhessen, Germany with Blauer Portugieser , Silvaner and Pinot Noir grapes.

Collo Tortonesi by I Carpini is a natural white wine made in the North of Italy, in Piedmont with Timorasso grapes. Simple, very clean white wine. Mineral touches, mildly floral with hint of vanilla. Some mild sulphur use but for this price no complaints

Kékburgundi 2022 by Franz Weninger is a natural red wine made in Burgenland with Pinot Noir grapes, which are called Kékburgundi in Hungarian where this wine is harvested (but vinified in Austria's Burgenland)
Hubertus Purus by Rudolf Trossen is a premium, no-added sulphur Riesling wine from the famous Mosel valley. This crisp white wine is vinified on two slate plots and aged in old German Foudre.

wine: Eschenhof Holzer - The Natural Orange 1 litre
notes: The Natural Orange by Eschenhofer Holzer, from Wagram in Austria is a natural wine surprisingly impressive for an easy, very affordable orange in 1 litre milk bottle! Made with Grüner Veltliner, this gives off an interesting nose of mint, wet grass and clementine. Easy breezy in mouthfeel, mild and good value considering its a whole litre.

Massale 2019 by Opi d'aqui is a natural wine made in Languedoc with three different types of Grenache; Grenache Gris , Grenache and Grenache Blanc grapes. This makes it a red white blend, and with an unusual chartacter.

wine: Manuel Pineau - Le Jardin de la Hyonnière Folle blanche 2021
notes: Le Jardin de la Hyonnière Folle blanche 2021 by Manuel Pineau is a natural wine made in Loire with Picpoule grapes.

wine: Manuel Pineau - Le Jardin de la Hyonnière Melon 2021
notes: Le Jardin de la Hyonnière Melon 2021 by Manuel Pineau is a natural wine made in Loire with Melon de bourgogne grapes.

Presto by Ab Initio is a natural white wine made with the creamy and equally refreshing Melon du Bourgogne, Chardonnay and Folle-blanche ( Piquepoul). Decant this one for best results to let the meadow flower aromas develop. We found it absolutely singing on the second day actually! Ab Initio is a Loire wine project involving winemaker Emmanuel Roblin as well as Fred and Claire Niger from esteemed Domaine de l’Ecu. Bottles are limited in quantity and despite being new and relatively unknown there is strong interest from winelovers!

wine: Christopher Barth - Rot vom Grun Nr 4
notes: Rot vom Grun nr 4 by is a natural wine made in Rheinhessen with Pinot Gris and Pinot Noir grapes, so this is a red white blend, hence the name. The wines from Christopher Barth are generally excellent value, light and refreshing. Production details of Rot vom Grun Nr 4: Rot vom Grun Nr 4 is made by Christopher Barth in the Rheinhessen region of Germany. The blend mixes Pinot Gris (Grauburgunder) and Pinot Noir, hence the name (a red-white blend). Christopher's natural wines are known for being light and easy-drinking. Tasting Notes: We have not yet tried this vintage of Rot vom Grun Nr 4 by Ch

Riesling 2020 by Max Dexheimer is a natural white wine made in Rheinhessen with 100% Riesling grapes, as the name suggests. This wine spends time on the lees, actually spending 18 months in the barrel

wine: Amelie Vuillet & Sebastien Jacques - Vin Dzi (ONE PER ORDER)
notes: Vin Dzi by Amelie Vuillet & Sebastien Jacques is a wine made in Jura with Savagnin grapes. This wine varies vintage to vintage but we find it to be an interesting take on Savagnin, perhaps more on the easier drinking, gluggable style than classic. WATCH OUR DOCUMENTARY ON THEM HERE

wine: Amelie Vuillet & Sebastien Jacques - Méli Mélo (one per order)
notes: Méli Mélo is a red/white field blend wine from Jura's Amelie Vuillet & Sebastien Jacques, featuring Savagnin, Ploussard, Trousseau and Chardonnay. Amelie Vuillet & Sebastien Jacques often focus on blends, as most of their vineyards are mixed varietals. This wine has a bright tartness to it. Being a big blend, its really quite unique for a Jura wine and thus should be drunk with this in mind. Wild and herbacious. Very fine, gentle sandy tannins. Serve very cold and enjoy One per order due to low production. WATCH OUR DOCUMENTARY ON THEM HERE

wine: Amelie Vuillet & Sebastien Jacques - Pif (one per order)
notes: Amelie Vuillet & Sebastien Jacques are small scale natural wine producers, who make natural wine without any sulphur in the Jura region of France. This Pif wine is a big red field blend, with great energy on the palate. WATCH OUR DOCUMENTARY ON THEM HERE
Max Dexheimer 'Pet Nat Weiss' is a sparkling wine made from Gelber Muskateller, Gewürtztraminer, Kerner, Müller-Thurgau, Silvaner. Super refreshing!

PIRI Naturel wines are made by young up-and-coming female producer Christine Pieroth, who is developing quite a buzz in Germany! This is her Pinot Noir, and it's both super juicy and elegant, very tasty indeed with a big depth of flavour and some earthy touches too. Quite cool!!!
Natural Wine producer Gregory White makes 'La Famille (1 Liter)' using grapes of Chenanson, which are grown in the Languedoc region of France.

Elle Aime by L'Octavin is a a natural wine, made with a blend of domain grapes of Pinot Noir and Chardonnay. This red/white blend from Jura is zippy and fresh, and featuring high acid! Watch our L'Octavin documentary here

Weissburgunder by Wasenhaus is a wonderful wine, by the highly sought-after winery from Baden, widely recognised amongst critics as being one of the most exciting low intervention producers in Germany. Having gained extensive experience in Burgundy, Christoph Wolber & Alexander Götze bring a unique Burgundian touch to German fine wines. VERY LIMITED. STRICTLY ONE PER ORDER

Franz Weninger's 'Rozsa Petsovits' is a beautiful dark rosé / light red made with Pinot Noir, Syrah, Blaufränkisch and Zweigelt... and it tastes Wunderbar! This wine has excellent value & excellent acidity. Great vibrations and bright energy. Expect vibrant dark cherry mingling with a touch of wood, hint of vanilla and herbs. Dark rosé but could act like a red. Interesting fact about Rosza Petsovits Rozsa Petsovits is really great value! And interestingly, the wine is named after Franz's grandmother, who was born in 1921 in Horitschon, then part of Hungary. This rosé is just as multicultural a

A Glimmer of Hops by Franz Weninger is a unique wine, as it is infused with Hops. Franz Weninger says: Around the fence of one of our orchards, wild hops settled down a few years ago. None of our beer brewer friends wanted to work with this wild hops. Therefore, we decided to process it ourselves: The fresh, uncooked hops was added to the wine during fermentation and remained with it for several weeks in the amphora. Since the wine was directly pressed Blaufränkisch, tannin and fruit on the palate of the Glimmer of Hops are attributed to the hops.

The Weninger Steiner site in Sopron is located in the south-western corner of Lake Neusiedl, on a slight slope to the east. In the Sopron annals, this vineyard was classified in 1680 as the best and most expensive vineyard in western Hungary (today's Burgenland). The gneiss and mica slate that comes to the surface makes the soil permeable, therefore dry and hot. Fourth Furmint vintage from the Steiner site. The barren soil of the site seems ideal for this strain. Unlike on the lime, it gets a slightly more mature, golden aroma here.
Tasty budget natural red from Austria's Weninger!

Ponzichter from Franz Weninger is an excellent value red , taken from vineyards in both Austria AND Hungary, as he has plots in both countries. The grapes are a combination of Blaufränkisch, Cabernet Franc, Pinot Noir and Zweigelt. The name actually comes from the German minority who used to grow wine there, and grew vegetables inbetween the vines, which the Hungarians mocked them for, calling them Ponzichter. This juicy, light wine is for lovers of Claus Preisinger’s Puszta Libre, as it shares some resemblance. Bright cherry and earthy hits with a touch of spice, all in tasty glouglou format

Blaufränkisch Hoch 2024 by Weninger is a natural wine made in Burgenland, and he Hochäcker site is one of the oldest vineyards in Horitschon. Its stoneless, hard, loamy subsoil is interspersed with iron. This makes it a traditional soil for Blaufränkisch. The vines are 40 years old. Franz Weninger states that this has notes of "Red berry fruit, fine forest berries, delicate hints of cherries, spices and tobacco. Freshly structured on the palate. A complex wine, but not opulent. Dense and extremely close-meshed, therefore easy to store."

Brand - Holy Chapel is a white wine made from Pinot Blanc (Weissburgunder) in the Pfalz region of Germany. This elegant yet raw and wild white wine is taken from a single vineyard plot, which really showcases their terroir and winemaking skill. We love it. So precise, so minerally and so balanced. Lengthy finish with clear malolactic vibes from long lees aging. A perfect Pinot Blanc (Weissburgunder) !!!

wine: Tenuta Vincenzo Nardone & Cantina Giardino - FxF
notes: Tenuta Vincenzo Nardone "FxF" is a lovely and aromatic orange wine from Campania, made of Fiano and Falaghnina grapes, which were actually made by both Tenuta Vincenzo Nardone and other Campanian winery Cantina Giardino, each vinifying their grapes and then blended together before bottling.

l'Americana 2020 by Tenuta Vincenzo Nardone is a bitter, tangy orange wine made in Campania, Italy with Greco grapes. The wine is made with carbonic maceration, and sees no additions of sulphites. Expect a little tannic grip and stone fruit touches dominant in the flavour profile.

Lafrea by Poderi Cellario is a fun, easy going natural wine made in the Langhe, a sub region of Piedmonte, Italy. La Favorita uses the grape Favorita, an old native grape variety of the Langa and Roero regions, well-adapted to poor, preferably sandy, soils. It was so named because it was once said to be a favored grape, particularly favored by King Vittorio Emanuele II. A straw-yellow wine, its bouquet is fruity and floral: hay, fresh flowers, and banana; on the palate, it is fresh and smooth, easy and unfussy

Nino Barraco 'Fior di Rosso' is made with Nero d’Avola, grown from the west coast of Sicily, Marsala to be precise. This has lovely touches of black cherry, eucalyptus and pepper on the nose and features a tasty prune and mild sour apple twang on the palate. Nice to have it at 12%, tasty stuff.
Rosato MAGNUM by Cantina Giardino is a red wine made in Campania with the regional Aglianico grapes.

Du Bicer Rosé (33cl) by Ferretti is a natural wine made in Emilia-Romagna with Lambrusco , Maestri and Salamino grapes. Du Bicer is a fun and cheerful Italian Pet Nat 'to go', ideal for times when one glass is enough or you fancy bringing something on the train to somewhere :)

Il Baffone, meaning "the moustache" by Podere Cellario is a sparkling pet nat wine from Veneto, Italy made using grapes of both Favorita and Moscato Bianco. These are quite aromatic grapes, so we expect bright floral tones and a herbacious quality to this Venetian pet nat!

Gaia 2019* by Cantina Giardino is a natural wine made in Campania with Fiano grapes. Gaia is a high acidic white with fresh aromatics and soft skin contact, with notes of apricot, cream popcorn, flowers and herbs.
Paski 2019* by Cantina Giardino is a natural wine made in Campania with Coda di Volpe grapes.
Volpe Rosa 2019* by Cantina Giardino is a natural wine made in Campania with Coda di Volpe grapes.
Pinot Nero 2019 by Bressan is a classic, quite collectable wine made in Friuli with Pinot Noir grapes, known in Italy as Pinot Nero. Expect rustic charm and a rich Italian soul ideal for aging

Chora Rosso by L'acino, is a lovely Italian red made from Magliocco grapes, soft and rounded with a tingly tannic structure, yet still light. This wine comes from the very hot region of Sourthern region of Calabria, where there is not much Natural Wine made, to be fair. Perfect with pizza and pasta. Production Details: Chora Rosso is a red wine from L'Acino in Emilia-Romagna made from a blend of local red grapes. Fermentation happens with native yeasts for an extended period on the skins — typically 4 to 6 weeks. The wine then ages in large wooden vessels, building complexity and texture witho

E´ Rosato (1 Liter) by Poderi Cellario is a natural wine made in Piedmont with Nebbiolo and Dolcetto grapes. Poderi Cellario state this is a Rosé wine produced from the bloodletting of two important vineyards. It remains on the skins for about a day, allowing it to ferment with its own yeasts. This wine is aged in cement vats; it is unclarified and unfiltered. On the nose, it releases red fruits and spices; the palate is fresh with a lovely tannin finish.

Bianco Anfora MAGNUM by Cantina Giardino is a natural wine made in Campania with Coda di Volpe , Falanghina and Fiano grapes. This Cantina Giardino wine, does not have any added Sulphites, like all their wines.

SIVI by Kemtijia Stekar is a delicious orange wine made from Pinot Grigio, in Slovenia. For those unaware, Pinot Grigio (aka Pinot Gris or Grauburgunder) is a pink skinned grape, which when macerated like an orange wine turns a beautiful and unique blush colour. Expect delightful notes of concentrated apricots, peaches and plums alongside a herbacious touch and vanilla cream finish. DELICIOUS! Watch a video review at the Colloseum here! Production Details: Located in the Brda region of Slovenia, Kmetija Stekar works with 5 hectares of vineyards. Sivi is a Pinot Grigio made as an orange wine th

E´ Orange (1 Liter) by Poderi Cellario is a natural wine made in Piedmont with Nascetta , Moscato Bianco and Incrocio Manzoni grapes. WOW! Talk about drinkability! This orange glouglou is just like breakfast juice, it's that damn gluggable. Watch out, dangerously easy drinking!!! Slightly aromatic and with a hint of honey on the finish. Little “body lotion” fun, clementines and citrus vibes. Remember to shake! As some vintages are less orange than this photographed vintage suggests

Drogone 2018 by Cantina Giardino is a natural wine made in Campania with Aglianico grapes, and no added sulphur. 2010 vintage: Earthy, complex, and with a clearly-aged flavour profile featuring notes of leather, plum & tobacco. This won't be for everyone but damn it sure kicks a punch for those who want this sort of wine. We enjoyed its complexity very much, but keep it for the right moment...

Derthona 2022 by Ricci is a natural wine made in Piedmont with Timorasso grapes. This rich, white wine ages for 12 months in used, 700 litre acacia wood barrels. Flavourwise it is creamy, full bodied and with low acidity, featuring a lovely minty note, alongside subtle flavours of melon and vanilla. Production Details: Derthona is a wine from the Piedmont region made from Barbera. The grapes are fermented with natural yeasts for approximately 30 days on the skins. Ageing takes place in large wooden barrels, allowing the wine to develop complexity whilst retaining the freshness and fruit charac
Dhyana 2021 by Valdibella is a simple natural Rosé wine made in Sicily with Perricone grapes made for fun afternoons. Expect red berries, hints of watermelon and vanilla

Zibibbo 2023 by Nino Barraco is a natural wine made in the Western part of Sicily next to Marsala. Here aromatic Zibibbo grapes, which are also known as Muscat d'Alexandria or Moscatel in other European countries, give of a large presence alongside a salty aspect with the vines being close to the sea. Expect big floral elements and extensive aromatics Production Details: Zibibbo is made from Grillo grapes grown in Marsala's hot, clay-limestone soils. Nino Barraco harvests ripe fruit and ferments with natural yeasts without added sulfites. The wine ages briefly in stainless steel, preserving th

Catarratto 2022 by Nino Barraco is a natural wine made in Sicily with the regional, often minerally and citrusy Catarratto grapes. Here the vines grow just a few hundred metres from the sea on volcanic soils giving a lot of tension and vibrancy to the wine.

Benedic 2020 by Monastero Trappiste Vitorchiano is a natural red wine made in Lazio with Sangiovese and Ciliegiolo grapes. The wine is made by Italian nuns, guided by natural winemaker Giampiero Bea. Tasting notes of Benedic 2020 from American wine importer Rosenthal: "The sisters produce a scant amount of red wine: a charming blend of equal parts Sangiovese and Ciliegiolo called “Benedic.” Despite a two-week maceration, “Benedic” is typically a beautifully pale, translucent wine. Registering just 11% alcohol, its color is calm, soft, and almost coppery—one can sense its gentle nature just fro

Coenobium Ruscum 2024 by Monastero Trappiste Vitorchiano is a natural wine made in Lazio with 45% Trebbiano , 35% Malvasia and 20% Verdicchio grapes. This white wine is grown and vinified by nuns in a monastary! This orange wine will have floral touches, nice aromatics and a slight tannic grip About Monastero Trappiste Vitorchiano - natural wines made by nuns! Amid Lazio’s volcanic tufa soils, the Cistercian Trappist nuns of Vitorchiano treat winemaking as a form of liturgy. Guided by Giampiero Bea, they hand-tend decades-old vines, ferment with wild yeasts and bottle without frills. The resul

Croci 'Valtolla' is a delightful, crunchy red blend of 60% Barbera and 40% Bonarda aka Croatina from Croci - perfect with cheeseboards or hearty pasta dishes! The grapes are macerated for 25-30 days on the skins and aged in cement vats. Croci states that Val Tolla was the ancient name for the middle Arda Valley, where vines have been cultivated since Roman times. It is made from Barbera and Bonarda (Croatina) grapes, traditionally grown on our hills. The fully ripe grapes are hand-picked into small crates and vinified by macerating on the skins for approximately thirty days. The rustic wine ex

Campedello by Croci is an unusual orange pet nat, with a cork. Bready, a bit meaty, grassy and tangy. Not for everyone, but very unique and interesting. A love it or hate it wine... For the grapes, here we have Malvasia di Candia 60%, Trebbiano e Ortrugo 35%, Sauvignon and Marsanne 5% which spend 7 days macerating on the skins. This Campedello wine which is a Colli Piacentini DOC spends 12 months in bottle before release, and is sparkling but not by a huge amount

wine: Podere Cipolla - Rosa Dei Venti Lambrusco
notes: Rosa Dei Venti Lambrusco by Podere Cipolla is a sparkling Lambrusco wine, made in Emilia-Romagna with Lambrusco Grasparossa and Malbo Gentile grapes. Absolutely delightful.

aromas: Raspberry, Sour Cherry, Mushroom, Limestone, Saline
notes: Saseti 2023 by Monte Dall´Ora is a natural wine made in Veneto with Corvina , Corvinone , Rondinella and Molinara Y Oseleta grapes. Perched on the limestone terraces of Castelrotto in the heart of Valpolicella Classica, Monte Dall’Ora farms its 25- to 70-year-old pergola-trained vines biodynamically, letting the “saseti” (“little stones”) in the soil shape the wine’s mineral pulse. Corvina and Corvinone dominate the field blend, rounded out by Rondinella, Molinara and the heirloom Oseleta, all harvested by hand from southeast-facing slopes between 70 – 200 m high. The 2023 was fermented sponta

Camporenzo 2020 by Monte Dall´Ora is a 13% natural red wine made in Veneto, Italy with 50% Corvina, 20% Corvinone, 20% Rondinella, 10% Molinara grapes. This wine ages for 10 months in 25-hl botti (wooden barrels made of Slovenian oak). After bottling, it ages for at least two years in the bottle before release. Expect a full body and smooth velvety finish Production Details: Camporenzo is a Valpolicella Superiore from a specific vineyard site. The blend of Corvina, Corvinone, Rondinella, and Oseleta reflects the terroir of the vineyard. Fermentation happens in stainless steel, followed by agei

Mongarda make high-quality Prosecco using the Charmant method (as well as Col Fondo, the ancient Pet Nat style). They farm 12 hectares and often do single vineyard plots in their bottlings, like the Extra Dry Valdobbiadene. The Vineyards here look beautiful and on well-exposed plots in the hills. This is a beautiful Prosecco using the traditional Glera grape - classic and clean yet still natural in feeling Production Details: This Prosecco from the Veneto region is made using the charmat method. Fermentation takes place in stainless steel pressure tanks, where the secondary fermentation create

Bolle Bandite by Gatti is a natural wine made in Veneto with Glera grapes. Working on a farm surrounded by animals, the wines of Carolina Gatti are rustic and approachable and at a good price too. Bolle Bandita is the name of her most well known wine, a Col Fondo Pet Nat featuring the Glera grape... so technically an old-school Prosecco. Except, it cannot be called Prosecco as not the legal style, so the name means "forbidden bubbles"...

É Rosso (1 Liter) by Poderi Cellario is a natural wine made in Piedmont with Barbera grapes. E Rosso is ideal as a table wine for BBQ or Pizza nights, and this is exactly what it was designed for, in a fun one litre bottle.

Cinino by La Segreta is a vibrant coloured Rosè wine made in Umbria, Italy with 100% Sangiovese grapes. The vines are grown on limestone and no added sulphites are used. Agri Segretum ( La Segreta) is located on 80 hectacres of olives, forest and plains in Collazzone, Umbria in Central Italy. 7.5 hectares of sunny southwest facing land Production Details: Cinino is a young wine from La Segreta in Sicily, made from indigenous grapes. The fruit ferments with natural yeasts in stainless steel or concrete, preserving freshness and acidity. The wine spends minimal time ageing, emphasising the prima

wine: La Via del Colle - Ambaradan Bianco 2020
notes: Ambaradan Bianco 2020 by La Via del Colle is a wine made in Emilia Romagna with Albana , Trebbiano and Pagadebit grapes.
Trebbiano by Casale is a traditional yet natural wine, is made in Tuscany with Trebbiano grapes.

Scirocco 2021 by La Via del Colle is an orange wine made in Emilia-Romagna, Italy with Pagadebit grapes. This wine is macerated on the skins for 15 days and aged for 6 months in Amphora, with no added sulphur. Expect some tannic grip here, making it ideal for food
Origine Rosso by Conti is a natural wine made in Piedmonte in the north of Italy with Nebbiolo and Vespolina grapes.
Giramondo by L'Acino is a white wine made in Calabria, Italy with aromatic Malvasia grapes.

Ego 2019 by Bressan is a cult, rare wine made in Friuli with Schioppettino and Cabernet Franc grapes. Whilst much of Friuli is focused on skin-contact amber wines, Bressan is known for his big reds. This wine will feature some peppery notes from the Cabernet Franc and bold, forest fruit touches from the Schioppettino. Production Details: Ego is a red wine from Bressan in Friuli-Venezia Giulia made from a blend of indigenous red grapes. Fermentation lasts 30 to 35 days on the skins with native yeasts. The wine then ages for an extended period in mixed wooden vessels — oak, chestnut, and wild pe
No3 2019 by Bressan is a natural wine made in Friuli with Pinot Noir , Cabernet Sauvignon and Schioppettino grapes. Expect this to be rustic, big, bold and full of Italian soul. This is a rare find.

Ognostro Bianco is a well-rounded italian white from Campania using the Fiano grape, with a slight touch of skin-contact. Expect notes of apricot, almonds, mint, bitter orange with white pepper tingling on the top of your palate. A tasty food wine where the alcohol is present in the taste but in an enjoyable way. About Marco Tinessa Marco Tinessa is a natural wine producer from the Campania region in Italy , although he actually used to be a banker in Milan - so quite the different life! Having received support from his mentor Frank Cornelissen, he decided to take on some land to preserve and

Bianco Frizzante by Cantina Giardino is a natural wine made in Campania, Italy with Coda di Volpe , Falanghina and Fiano grapes. It's not common to see a sparkling wine from Cantina Giardino. This one is rather tasty with a slight 'twang' to it, as we recall.

Amico Frizz by Castello Di Stefanago is a natural wine made in Lombardia with Riesling grapes, which is not a common find in Lombardia. Production details of Amico Frizz: Amico Frizz comes from Castello di Stefanago in the Oltrepò Pavese hills of Lombardia, run by brothers Antonio and Giacomo Baruffaldi. The Castello has stood since the 11th century and the family farms 20 hectares of vines across small scattered plots within a 135-hectare estate. The Riesling here is made by the ancestral method with refermentation in bottle, and bottled under crown cap with no added sulphur. Tasting Notes: W
Tu Tu by Cantina Giardino is a natural wine made in Campania with Fiano grapes. Tu Tu is an easy going, very drinkable wine served in a litre bottle, for extra fun!

Cantina Giardino 'Rosso Magnum' is made with Aglianico grapes, and is usually an assemblage of vintages making it a Non-Vintage wine. Long maceration on the skins, no added sulphur and a nice drinkability make the Cantina Giadino magnum a good fit for a BBQ or dinner party.

El Matt by Ricci is a more classic styled, red natural wine, with elegance and Italian charm. El Matt is made using 100% Croatina grapes from Piedmonte, more specifically the T ortonese area. This rich and deep 15% red wine is in steel in order to enhance freshness. This rustic red has big fruit notes of pomegante and cherry with a hint of earth, and finalising with a finish of light licorice. This one is big at 15% and for tannin lovers

Renosu Bianco by Dettori is a natural wine made in Sardinia, Italy with Vermentino and the aromatic Moscato Giallo grapes. Dettori state their Renosu Bianco is " an intensely aromatic wine, straight forward and uncomplicated, pure pleasure in a wineglass. Enjoy chilled. Renosu, which in our local language mean sandy, is not new, but traditional here: marrying together complex acidity with the intense sweetness is a pleasurable custom. Renosu Bianco expresses a singular coppery golden colour, crystalline and bright. The nose presents fine and fragrant scents of ripe pear, nectarine, white flowe

Renosu Rosso by Dettori is a natural wine made in Sardinia, Italy with Grenache (Cannelou), Monica and Pascale grapes. This is a nicely extracted wine, very fruit forward with a touch of mild residual sugar, which works well. Here a slight earthy, mushroom taste that works well. Dettori state that "Renosu Rosso is our everyday red wine—-fragrant, simple, natural, the red wine to uncork with friends, for a wine glass brimming with pleasure. Renosu, which means sandy in our language, was born from the idea of the traditional custom, for everyday wines, of combining wines of different red grapes.

This is the formally known Vignamare from Nino Barraco, who is based close to Marsala in Sicily. This refreshing and saline white wine is now called Biancammare. The Grillo vines roots reach right to the sea, and many vintages offer a strong sense of salinity, hence the name. Expect classical finesse alongside saline touches and a nice natural energy. Sicily in a glass! Production Details: Biancammare is a Grillo from Marsala in Sicily. The vineyard soils are clay and limestone. Nino Barraco practices organic methods in the vineyard and natural winemaking in the cellar. The wine ferments witho
Rosammare 2022 by Nino Barraco is a natural wine made in the Marsala region of Sicily with Nero D’Avola grapes, which are harvested earlier giving this wine some tannic, dark fruity character.

Nero D´Avola 2022 by Nino Barraco is a natural wine made in the Marsala region of Sicily with red Nero D’Avola grapes, typical to the island. This wine is known to features notes of Mullberry and Cocoa.

Nino Barraco is one of the pioneers of natural wine in Sicily, but rather than other local superstars in Etna or Alcamo, he is more lonesome over in Marsala. A region famed for fortified wine production.. of which a HUGE portion made is actually only used as cooking wine! We visited the estate before we had fully set up MORE Natural Wine, and we impressed to see some vineyards have roots reaching literally into the sea! Some may argue this gives the wines a salinity, whilst others will argue in the name of science that this is technically impossible to get flavours delivered from root to grape

Ognostro by Marco Tinessa is a natural wine made in Campania with Aglianico grapes.
