This year’s Otium is an infusion of grenache noir, (90% of the wine) picked from 80 year old selection massale vines planted by Laurent’s grandfather in Espira d’Agly. Laurent says it’s an old variety of grenache with nowhere near as strong a colour as newer clones and very little tannin, which allows the complexities the soil offers to be better expressed. It was infused for 11 days with grenache gris from the Fourques vineyard the previously Alain Castex farmed and aging was in a concrete tank which fittingly belonged to Castex. It is pink and we possibly should have it as a rosé. The pinkne

Idoine, as usual, is 100% Merlot. It comes from 30 year old vines in Rivesaltes planted by Laurent’s father on quite heavy clay soils. His meticulous pruning in this vineyard, and then strict disbudding each spring is, Laurent thinks, contributing to more maturity each year, and it’s visible in the glass. Although it’s juicy, there is plenty of structure as well. Whole bunches were macerated for a few days and it was aged in a mix of fibreglass and barrels. “It’s our gamay” according to Laurent. And, because it’s not as dark as last year’s vintage, it’s another one of our new ‘dark, light red’

The wine is made from approximately 70 year old macabeu vines growing on clay and rolled pebbles of limestone in Espira-de-l’Agly. The vines were planted by Laurent’s grandfather but they purchased the vineyard from a subsequent owner a few years ago, at the time without knowing who had planted them. It is a mix of approximately 50/50 directly-pressed and macerated juice. But the short 5 day maceration was not with the purpose of making an orange wine. Laurent feels thar this period of maceration helps the finished wine to express some of the soil’s complexities and also is insurance for a goo

wine: 78 Degrees Distillery The Italian Australian Bitter Orange
notes: The orange bitter uses native Australian botanicals, riberries, thyme, lime and quandong, alongside traditional European botanicals. It is the perfect balance between Campari and Aperol. Best served in a Spritz or Negroni.

Wiradjuri Country. Sangiovese grown in Mudgee. Raspberry and cola with an effortless dry finish, serve chilled for maximum fun drinking. A parcel of these grapes were harvested earlier for direct press rosato style and then the remaining grapes when picked a little fuller in ripeness and fermented with native yeast in an open top fermenter. Gentle plunges only then pressed from skins within 7 days. The two parcels were then blended together resulting in a lighter style wine that is aromatic and crunchy. … and yes this wine is absolutely named after Rizzo from Grease - Samantha May
Tags: Australia, Ephemera, Pinot Noir, Victoria, Yarra Valley

grapes: Pinot Noir, Syrah, Shiraz, Pinot Gris
notes: Creative flair has always been the metier of Konpira Maru and here they blend five different varieties from five vineyards to create a super blend (like the 1980s space explorers who combined in the TV series of the same name). It’s quietly complex, very juicy, easy drinking in style and generally a lot of fun. It’s all sloshy textured but with crunchy, red berry fruit and sweet/floral detail. It feels more juice than wine in some respects, and fittingly comes with incredible drinkability.

Wurundjeri Country This riesling, pinot gris and gewurztraminer field blend is from the Merkel Vineyard that straddles the ridge (~550m above sea level) running up to Mount Bellevue on a forgotten outpost of Whitlands. Tropical acid! Dried apple, pineapple, a bit of paw paw and some sharp apricot. Then throw in some electric acidity, not sour acid, yummy, saliva inducing acid. Literally impossible to drink a bottle in more than 20 minutes(by yourself) excepting some sort of epic tantric mind control. - Konpira Maru

Kaurna Country Dry on the tongue, but it's a very wet wine. A visceral medley of passion, indulgence and spaghetti alle vongole. Nebbiolo and Sangiovese from the Barossa, plus a little Sangiovese from the Hills, gently made under the sultry supervision of Monica Bellucci. - Giovanni Armani Giorgio

Wurundjeri Woi Wurrung Country A blend of cabernet sauvignon and pinot noir, which would likely have the toffs reeling due to the 'crossing of the streams' of Bordeaux and Burgundy's finest red varieties, but no issue for the playful, avant garde of Bobar. This is a lighter weight red, not transparent, but swishy and red fruited, lashed with truffle and dried, Italian herb notes, a squish of blood orange to close. Chillable as. Drink without a chill, fine also. Go forth.

Wurundjeri Woi Wurrung Country A blend of chardonnay, sauvignon blanc and viognier to produce a textural, salty white wine! Here's what the winemakers say: A fresh, textured and saline white, extremely versatile for food pairing and downright delicious. Beurre Bosc pear, white flowers, fleshy white and yellow nectarine, marzipan and wet stone. A blend of varieties, and a blend of techniques. The Chardonnay was direct pressed and barrel fermented, the Sauvignon Blanc given a short amount of skin contact before pressing and barrel fermentation, and the Viognier carbonic macerated for 7 days befo

Peramangk Country Everyone's favourite cosmic cat is back outta the bag! Living legend James Erskine's shiraz/grenache blend is a perennial favourite, and this year's release is no exception. The best of both varieties: big, bold red fruit and peppery spice joining forces in a slurpy, juicy red with crunchy texture that's primed for a light chill. As always, no sulphur...but lots of deliciousness!

Kaurna Country and Peramangk Country Who doesn't love Danby? James Erskine's carbonic grenache is back in full force in 2024. Light, bright, skippy as all get-out and full of energy. Fruit-forward, packed with r aspberries and christmas spices , but balanced with a good dose of rocky minerality. Chill it right down and drink it right up!

The world's best Bloody Mary mix, made from scratch in our very out back yard ... well Redfern. Makes 3 small / 2 medium or 1 maxi-Mary, just add your favourite white spirit. We like a liberal splash of Poor Tom's Sydney Gin in ours. A cause AND a cure. May as well get 2 !

aromas: Blackberry, Lemon, Chamomile, Ginger, Thyme, Rosemary
notes: Discover L'Antidote: a sparkling and natural drink, born from the perfect balance between 70% juice (grape and apple) and 30% infusion of organic herbs – ginger, lemon, yarrow, poppy, rosemary, thyme, mallow, blackberry, agrimony and verbena. A lively and refreshing attack, driven by perfectly balanced acidity. Fresh fruit flavors mingle harmoniously with herbal infusions like basil and chamomile, offering a subtle and soothing complexity. Fine bubbles add a sparkling and festive touch, while the delicate bitterness on the finish prolongs the sensation of freshness. A refined and healthy alter

L'Antilope, little sister of L'Antidote, is a unique creation, born from the subtle balance between 70% infusion of organic plants and 30% fruit juice (grape and apple). Its composition showcases refined, natural aromas: woody and aromatic notes of juniper, pine, and bay leaf, balanced by a slight bitterness from gentian and yarrow. With 50% less sugar than Antidote and a beautiful golden hue, L'Antilope offers a healthy and sophisticated alternative. The Antelope is elegance in all its simplicity, to be enjoyed at any time! Perfect with aged cheeses, light desserts, or even savory dishes feat

Nyctalope is a bolder and more expressive variation of L'Antilope. It comes from the subtle blend of 70% organic plant infusion and 30% fruit juice (grape and apple) , worked like a wine, in a search for balance between freshness, bitterness and tension. Its composition highlights notes of bitter orange, enhanced by Sichuan pepper and supported by a herbaceous and floral base of verbena and yarrow. Darker and spicier than L'Antilope, Nyctalope explores a deeper register, with a pronounced yet elegant bitterness. Nyctalope is the expression of another facet of the plant world: wild, intense and

wine: Aubert & Mathieu Baburu Cremant de Limoux NV
notes: Savor the elegance of our Crémant de Limoux, a refined and precise expression of the renowned appellation. Each glass reveals a bouquet of intense aromas of crisp lemon, harmoniously balanced by seductive acidity and gourmet nuances of hazelnut and pastry. The tasting continues with a delicately fine and persistent foam, leading to a dazzlingly pure finish. - Aubert & Mathieu

aromas: White Peach, Peach, Lemon, Orange Blossom, Saline
notes: GIGI is Aubert & Mathieu's take on Albariño, an organic white wine that combines finesse, freshness, and a saline character. From the first whiff, it offers delightful aromas of white peach, candied lemon, and orange blossom. On the palate, it's taut and vibrant, with a silky texture and a briny finish that prolongs the pleasure. A mineral and elegant wine, perfect for any table that dares to taste what's right. - Aubert & Mathieu

NUBA, a certified organic natural wine with no added sulphites, embodies the quintessence of natural wine. Discover its lively and juicy flavors of wild strawberries, cherries and raspberries, demonstrating authentic freshness and fruitiness. Ideal as an accompaniment to cold cuts, tapas or a tasty ratatouille, NUBA is a perfect choice for convivial and gourmet moments. Savor every sip of NUBA, a wine that honors nature and artisanal know-how, reflecting the best of the terroir. - Aubert & Mathieu
Tags: France, Provence

wine: Churton Wines Natural State Pinot Noir 2024
notes: 2024 Pinot Noir is classic Churton wine, Damson plum fruitiness leads to aromatic dried rose bud, violets and spice in the aroma. in the mouth the wine is fine with soft and smooth fruit of dark plums and wonderful chalky mouth feel great length with spice and vitality. Delicious - Churton Wines

wine: Churton Natural State Pied de Cuve Sauvignon Blanc 2022
notes: Our Natural State pied de cuve is alive. It is a wine that takes the characters of the vineyard and brings them to life creating new dimensions and complexity. Our 2019 pied de cuve is fresh, fruity and full of texture, citrus fruit from start to finish with glimpses of wild flowers. Acidity and texture are the back bone to this autumn meets spring wine. - Churton

wine: Dear Vincent Pink Cowboy Chilled Red NV
notes: Kambuwal Country. Pink Cowboy = you, a group of mates, warm summer's day, long lunch (or in the pool). It’s super juicy, generous and dangerously sessionable. Made with nebbiolo, cabernet, along with some chard and pinot gris thrown in all off our Vineyard. It’s been the biggest selling wine for me all year and for good reason! Serve chilled (fridge/esky cold). Pair with beach days, some KFC fried chicken, lamb salad at lunch, a bucket of prawns, or nothing at all….. Pink Cowboy rides solo just fine. More slippery than satin sheets on a Sunday. Get amongst it. Summer is calling! - Dear Vincent

Kambuwal Country. I'd literally put Chardonnay on my Wheetbix if it was socially acceptable. I just love a good chard. We have two big blocks of Chardonnay here at the St Judes vineyard - one at the top of the hill and the other at the bottom of the hill. We make a contemporary chard - not one that you'll find in nannas wine rack, the style that went out with her shoulder pads and perm. It's bright and zippy, fun and minerally. Actually banging with garlic prawns... even more banging with the Ndjua Scallops (or oysters) at Josies... IYKYK. Super yum. We love it. - Dear Vincent

Just like the VN red, the white is made in a similar style. Again seven different varieties are used, including garnatxa blanca, macabeu, moscatell, pansé, parrellada, vinyater and xarel-lo. These grapes varieties are kept on whole bunch until the first signs of fermentation. Massimo believes that this is the best way to extract to delicate aromas and flavours left over from the flowering of the vine. This is quite evident in this wine with definite hint of florals on the nose, leading into a fresh, briny and vibrant palate. A joy to drink.

80% gamay and 20% grolleau. A portion of the gamay was directly pressed, the majority de-stemmed, the two components put together for fermentation. The grolleau was macerated separately, both varieties for 10 days, with blending occurring after pressing and before élevage. - Vivant Selections, importer Medium bodied and red-fruited, with fine dusty tannins and a savoury earthy backbone underpinned by bright acidity.

Garnacha Tinta, Garnacha Blanca. Claret is a type of wine made by blending red and white grapes. In this case, it is produced by the co-fermentation of two parts Garnatxa Blanca and one part Garnatxa Tinta. It is a type of traditional wine, originating from certain regions of Spain, fresh, easy to drink with a unique color. Vinified in stainless steel tanks. - Partida Creus

Ve d’Avior is the personal project of Cati Ribot, a third generation grape farmer, the inaugural vintage in 2019. Her family's 14 hectare estate, Galmes I Ribot, is located in Santa Margalida, North East Mallorca. An island bathed in sunshine, the summers are hot, the winters mild. The soils are iron-rich clay with a lot of calcareous rocks. - Liz Carey, importer After gradually taking the reigns at her family winery, she began to convert all the farming to organic. Cambuix is a blend of native varieties escursac, callet, callet negro and monto negro. This summertime smasher is loaded with rhu

Zvari is 100% rkatsiteli that sees one week of skin contact and is then aged in tank for nine months and is held in bottle for another year before release. Golden pear, walnut and green tea. Big and juicy, cuddly orchard fruits and the gentlest tug of tannin. Soft acidity, quinine biter refreshment to finish. Clean and bright, a crowd pleaser.
Ngunnawal County. 100% carbonic maceration for two months. Gentle extraction, with maturation in older barriques and ceramic. Juicy red cherry, dried herbs and crushed gravel. - Mada Wines

Peramangk Country A fragrant, vibrant and juicy Nero from the Adelaide Hills. A nod to the fragrant and energetic Nero / Frappato based blends from Sicily, where Parish Hills 550m elevation provides the freshness in this wine. De-stemmed and fermented on skins for 3 weeks. Pressed to a few year old foudre where it matured for 12 months. - Steve Crawford, wine maker

Peramangk Country 60% Vermentino & 40% Inzolia - all from the Parish Hill Vineyard in Uraidla, Adelaide Hills. All hand picked separately, with a day or two of maceration post de-stemming. Fermented in neutral oak and left on lees for 8 months. All adding to the texture and structure. Bright acid and salty minerality. Enjoy with some snacks or food, preferably with the ocean in sight. - Steve Crawford, winemaker

Lutruwita Country. Dr Edge 'Ambrosia' is a blend of schonburger and pinot gris fruit from The Tamar Valley. Co-fermented on skins for one week, its pressed to old oak casks to dry out and relax for two months, then bottled without filtration. Ambrosia is a sexually confused robot who thinks it is immortal. - Peter Dredge
A blend of grenache blanc and direct press grenache noir. Saline, white peach and toasted baguette dominate the palate. Hints of aniseed and texture for days. Yes please!

The amazing Zibibbo grape, also known as Muscat de Alexandria, is organically grown in marsala, western Sicily. The COS windery dates back to the 1880's and has been farmed organically since the 1980's. This wine is fermented on skins in terracotta amphorae buried underground, giving this wine a beautifully aromatic nose. Structured notes of citrus zest, orange blossom and a mineral chalky texture. Drink this with some seafood!

An equal parts blend of grecanico and insolia from the Sicilian legends at COS. This wine is fermented on skins and has a beautiful early sunset orange colour, with aromas of orange-blossom, apple cider and marzipan. Some fresh apricot and peach notes are balanced with a green tea tannic feel. Finishing with honey and jasmine - absolutely beautiful. Iconic and not to be missed.

COS has been a trailblazer in Sicily’s burgeoning natural wine scene since 1980. Frappato is a rare, indigenous varietal that produces light-bodied, elegant and aromatic wines. This is ruby red, smooth as silk and elegant drinking with the freshness and vibrancy of wild strawberries alongside the sweet warmth of nutmeg and cinnamon spices.

wine: Bois Moze Cremant de Loire Brut NV
notes: All chenin blanc in an exciting, delicious, quietly complex sparkling wine from Loire Valley. Geez, we love Cremant de Loire, so much bang for buck, that swish of saline minerality, the touch of sea spray, the vibrancy of chenin blanc citrus, stone fruit and green apple freshness. It's a masterclass in awesome sparkling wine right here. Fancy and interesting.

Ward means "rose" in Arabic, a name that perfectly captures the delicate beauty and playful spirit of this wine. Made from Syrah grapes, Ward is a fresh and vibrant rosé with delicate red berry aromas, floral notes and a refreshing finish. Light, elegant and effortlessly drinkable, it's the kind of wine that brings a little sunshine to any occasion. From long summer lunches to spontaneous evenings with friends, Ward is a reminder to slow down and enjoy life's little pleasures. Fresh, floral and full of life. Just like a rose in bloom. - Olea & Vine, Importers

Nour means "light" in Arabic, a name inspired by the warmth, beauty and energy of the land where our wines are born. Made from indigenous Lebanese Obeideh and White Grenache grapes, Nour is a natural white wine that brings together freshness, delicate stone fruit flavours and a beautiful texture developed through amphora aging. Grown in the Lebanese mountains and made with minimal intervention, Nour reflects our desire to let the grapes and the land speak for themselves. A little light, a little warmth, and a beautiful expression of our Lebanese roots. - Olea & Vine, Importers

wine: Wedded to the Weather Barrel Select Lagrein 2024
notes: Peramangk, Ngadjuri and Kaurna country. Lagrein getting a pure chance at freshness in a bottle. Mulberry, inky blueberry, plush texture, soft feels. Yum. Just yum. Not trying too hard, just pure fruit, softness, good sense of lift. A bit of liquorice and faint seaweed character, a touch of grunty tannin late in the piece. Above and beyond, a straight up chillable red of fresh feel and purity. You’d crack this in the morning for its digestible, energetic nature and be good. If not, just a party in the glass. - The Wine Front

Cloudy and textural, this is old vine korinta with skin contact from Chilean winemaker Gustavo Martinez. There's plenty of structure and complexity here, leesy and pithy but lifted by grapefruit and floral notes and hints at tropical fruits. Real good food wine.

A skinsy orange wine that passes the two-glass test. Pecorino and Malvasia were co-fermented on skins, then splashed with Grenache Blanc for flesh and freshness. Golden, tropical and slightly unhinged — like dessert that forgot it was wine. Mango steen, guava and pineapple up front, with peach underneath and a lemony lift. The palate is ripe stone fruit with a gentle tannic grip. Wait… is that orange Tic Tacs? - Table Wines

wine: Tim Ward I'll Fly Away Lambrusco Rifermentato NV
notes: Quite a classic style of Lambrusco, full bright cherry fruits mingled with earth and charcuterie, it has a delightful bubble and a dry finish. Serve well chilled with a plate of mortadella or your favourite pizza. Perfetto!! - Tim Ward, winemaker

wine: Tim Ward Wines Still Maestri Lambrusco 2025
notes: A table wine from lambrusco. From Chalmers Vineyard. Delicious, fresher expression on hand. Scents of dark cherry, black olive, salted plums. Flavours very similar, a smudge of gentle tannin, bright acidity under the darker, saline fruitiness, easy to drink, charming straight up. High enjoyment factor in a vibrant, brighter, medium weight style. - The Wine Front

wine: Tim Ward I'll Fly Away If I Had Wings Greco 2022
notes: From Heathcote. The fruit is kept on skins for three weeks through fermentation, then pressed off and spends two years in old oak. About 8 months in bottle before release. Proper orange winemaking. A textural feast! Delicious and refreshing under chalky texture, dried citrus, mandarin juice, touches of curry spice, floral things. Wonderful!

wine: Tim Ward I'll Fly Away With Mrs Woo Pet Nat 2023
notes: Wonnarua Country A collab wine for the beautiful folk at High Tea With Mrs Woo. Chardonnay from Pokolbin. Twelve months on full lees for a more serious (in the best possible way) pet nat. Tim says " Best enjoyed with family. friends, food and frivolity."

wine: Tim Ward I'll Fly Away Bianco Vermentino 2025
notes: The wine sees a two day skin ferment but ends up cloudy, hazy and with chewy pucker and a nice grip to texture. Lots of dried citrus, a touch of earthy savouriness, dried herbs, mandarin and tonic water characters in the mix too. It's a lighter version of orange wine with lots of energy and plenty of interest. A little wilder edged, in a great sense. Go forth.

wine: Tim Ward I'll Fly Away Bianco Ancestral 2025
notes: Wurundjeri Country 60% vermentino skin fermented for a cuppla days and blended with 40% direct press fiano and boom, sent to bottle to keep on fizzing au naturale and hence we have a pet nat. It's a lively, squeaky-textured number, bright and vivacious with faint nutty-saline characters amongst bruised lime, green apple and nectarine fruit stuff going on. Fizz is big, bold, refreshing. It's a ripper.

aromas: Green Apple, Sea Spray, Saline, Almond
notes: One of those wines that we say 'saline, textural white wine' as a quip, but in longer format explain that the wine is medium bodied, has a slipperiness then chalky pucker while showing off amazing, saline and brine minerality at its core. Yes thanks! Tonic water and hazy green apple juice with some sea spray and green almond - that's the roll call of descriptors. From one of South Africa's leading (and original) lights of avant garde wines.

Summer Berry Horchata is a blend of locally grown blueberries, raspberries, blackberries and strawberries, blended with local organic rice and infused with allspice and nutmeg. The result is a lavishly creamy, luxe shrub that makes you think of fruits of the forest or berry sorbet. Inspired by the fruity rice based Aqua Fresca that is served as a welcome drink and daily thirst quencher in Mexico and South America. Horchata is a sweet, slightly creamy, totally luxurious, spiced and fruity dream come true. It originated in the Middle East and Africa, where nuts and various grains were blended in

When it's hot do you like to stay cool? Do you like drinks refreshing but not too sweet? Do you like words like crisp, fresh and hydrate? Do you like the colour pink? Do you like gin? This shrub is all colour and depth. Serve with gin or stand alone. - Pyewacket's

For the lovers of agave spirits- this shrub was designed to be the perfect complement. Mango smoothes the smokey qualities of mezcal. Lime brightens the piquant nature of tequila. Fresh jalapeno for warmth and base. Serve as a margarita soda with a salted rim, or just a splash in a shot of good spirit, sipped. - Pyewacket's
Strong and of the earth. The heaviest of citrus fortified with the spices of an ancient medicine chest. A warriors drink. Dry Russian vodka or stand alone. Drink hot or cold. - Pyewacket's

Wonnarua Country The Harkham shiraz wines sit outside the tried and tested, rote at times red wines of Hunter, happily more abundant, less primped and preened, natural in their expressions. This wine continues the legacy. Oh, and Kosher certified, and preservative free too. The latter something Harkham has mastered over many years. It’s a looser knit, sappy and savoury red wine, a sluice of wild raspberry, wild cherry, violet florals, dried herbs, white pepper, touches of game meat, some bergamot notes and a slosh of mulberry/’purple’ going on. It marches to its own beat, feels nourishing and

wine: Wedded To The Weather Evening Breeze Fridge Red #1 2026
notes: Peramangk, Ngadjuri and Kaurna Country. This one is montepulciano from organic vines. From the once was backyard Brisbane winemaker, now doing his thing during harvest in the Barossa Valley. Lovely stuff. Crunchy texture, bright, cherry fruitiness, some cranberry drink freshness, a little cola character. It’s easy going, loose knit in a way, gorgeous and pure. This one definitely should be drunk cold to get its best, sitting at a few pay grades up from rosé as it is. Yum. - The Wine Front

wine: Wedded To The Weather Cloud Project Sea Breeze Picpoul 2025
notes: Wedded to the Weather blasts in value and interest, shoots from the hip with edgy styles, delivers on freshness and vitality in its wines. Lesser sung varieties are a calling card, drinkability written into the DNA of the wines. Simple, done well, and accessible. From organic certified fruit of the Riverland. Pitch perfect seaside white vibe here. Squeaky lemon drink, tonic water, saline minerality, cucumber – not particularly complex but all the right moves. A gentle bitterness in the pleasing slosh and crackle of the wine. Big refreshment factor. Truly delicious. - The Wine Front

wine: Wedded to the Weather Cloud Project Summer Haze Fernao Pires 2026
notes: New from the quixotic wine collection of Doug Woodward, he of Brisbane wine retail landscape, married to legendary meteorologist and journalist Jenny Woodward for ABC Brisbane. Hence the name. Doug has moved operations to the Barossa Valley and a co-op winery that draws in a variety of winemakers of varying styles. This wine follows on from Doug’s interest in skin fermentation and lesser known varieties grown organically in Riverland. Here fernao pires, the Portuguese white variety, gets a go. Fruit juice! Fun fruit juice! Spice fruit juice! A kind of tart, drying tannin profile in it all too.

wine: Wedded to the Weather Barrel Select Prieto Picudo 2023
aromas: Raspberry, Dark Chocolate, Sage, Mint, Fennel
notes: Peramangk, Ngadjuri and Kaurna country. Unique variety, from Spain but off the Bassham Vineyard in Riverland. Soupy and rich, a dark fruited, sweet fruited red but also with some curious, piquant, peppery notes and leafy green herb characters in there too. Dark chocolate-dipped raspberries, cola, mint and fennel, game meat, raspberry and cream lollies, a bit of sage leaf too. Some chewy tannin, slightly silty in its way. Black tea in the mix too, some smoky tea characters too. Quite exotic, but the drinkability is high. - The Wine Front

wine: Wedded to the Weather Barrel Select Durif 2023
notes: Peramangk, Ngadjuri and Kaurna country. Doug Woodward now makes wines in the Barossa Valley, a fair way away from his back of house winemaking in Brisbane. Growing up. Thick and rich, stand a spoon up in it kind of feel. Soft plum, prune nectar, sweet spices, milk chocolate, green olive and salt bush characters. So potent, but so enticing and has super high drinkability in its way. Magic neck oil. Lush and yum. - The Wine Front

wine: Women's Work Date, Tomato & Ginger Relish 330g
notes: Date, Tomato & Ginger Relish is a rich, jammy relish made with sweet dried dates, ripe tomatoes, fresh ginger and a delicate hint of chilli. Slowly cooked for an almost caramelised depth, it balances sweetness with savoury flavour and gentle warmth. Made for anyone looking for something beyond a traditional tomato relish, it is exceptionally versatile. Spoon it beside curry, dhal, samosas or savoury rice. Pair it with sharp cheddar or creamy blue on a cheese board. Spread it generously through a sandwich or ham and cheese toastie, or serve it alongside pies, cold meats and roast pork. - Women'

wine: Domaine Vincent Carême Vouvray Le Clos 2023
notes: Le Clos is a 2.30 ha plot surrounded by walls built in the 16th century and adjoining an old castle that is part of the same locality. As its name suggests, this fence symbolized a boundary to prevent any thief or predator from accessing the precious grapes. The 60-year-old vines are located on the first west-facing slopes overlooking the Brenne valley. The shallow clay-limestone soil will give density and structure to the wine, with great aging potential. A rich nose with aromas of pear and acacia, the palate is structured with notes of quince and a touch of smoke, and a saline finish is obse

wine: Domaine Vincent Carême Vouvray Brut Nature 2023
notes: Made from a blend of young and old vines, this traditional method cuvée is primarily produced using the grapes' natural sugars. Alcoholic fermentation takes place in temperature-controlled fiberglass tanks and is stopped at 18g of residual sugar. A reserve wine of 10 to 15% is added before bottling. The second fermentation occurs in the bottle, followed by aging on lees for 12 to 24 months. After disgorgement, this wine is not dosed. An expressive nose with notes of peach and white flowers; the palate is delicate and persistent, with subtle aromas of toasted almond. A wine with fine bubbles, f

This naturally sparkling rosé is made from a blend of red grape varieties - 40% cabernet franc, 40% malbec, 20% gamay, 20% grolleau - giving it freshness and deliciousness. Fine bubbles, fruity and fresh. Rich and refreshing on the palate. Aromas of red fruits, strawberry, redcurrant. - Vincent Carême

Coming from different plots with distinct terroirs (flint clay, limestone), this cuvée offers a classic Vouvrillonne expression. The nose has slightly smoky notes with aromas of vine peach, the palate is fruity and expressive with citrus notes. - Vincent Carême

Peramangk Country. McLaren Flat is the source. Organic farmed. Skins for two months. Old oak. Chewy and yet slender tannins, a savouriness distinct in the wine, rose water, dried cranberry, cherry, rose hip tea and dusty spice. Some hazelnut notes in the mix, an Italianate bent to the wine, soft, slurpy finish with a little gravelly grip. A bounciness to the wine, a seriousness to tannin, and a delightful palate reset in that too. Intriguing. - WineFront.com.au

wine: Frankly, This Wine Was Made by Tom 2023
producer: Frankly This Wine was Made By Bob
notes: Wiradjuri and Ngurra Country Every year we try to maintain an open mind and experiment with different portions of vineyards and with different varieties. Often these experiments make it into our single variety or single vineyard wines. We then blend a portion of all the different experimental wines into one whacky blend, this is what has come to be known as Tom wine. The beauty of this wine is that it's different every vintage. This year the Tom wine is whole bunch sauvignon blanc, full carbonic syrah, and shiraz rose that has been fermented on chardonnay skins. This wine is low alcohol, super

producer: Frankly This Wine was Made By Bob
notes: Bob has done it again ! This is the red wine you want when you want a red wine for the fridge, to splash around into a couple of tumblers and share with friends. Get amongst it before it's all gone.

producer: Frankly This Wine was Made By Bob
notes: Ngurra Country. Picpoul, riesling and semillon but honestly, does that even matter? All grapes here were destemmed and fermented separately for a month before being pressed to puncheons. Only 6 months on full fermentation lees before bottling. This excellent wine is perfect whether served at room temperature or chilled in the fridge. It offers refreshing notes of orange sherbet, complemented by a delightful herbal undertone. - Frankly Bob team

producer: Frankly This Wine was Made By Bob
notes: Primitivo, cabernet sauvignon and merlot rose from the Cargo Road vineyard in Orange. The primitivo was picked earlier and the other two a little later which created an ultra-refreshing acidity with plenty of textural omphy purple fruit flavours. Superbly thirst-quenching rose for all occasions.

producer: Frankly This Wine was Made By Bob
grapes: Chardonnay, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Sauvignon Blanc
notes: Ruby is a 50/50 blend of pinot gris and merlot rose that has been fermented on sauvignon blanc, chardonnay and verdelho skins. Lifted stone fruits, as well as lovely raspberry notes. Delicious. Light red or rose....you choose!!

wine: Gabriel Boudier Crème de Cacao White Liqueur
notes: Derived from the Crème de Cacao 25%, the White Crème de Cacao 15% embodies the craftsmanship and precision of Maison Gabriel Boudier. Smooth, balanced, and completely colorless, it reveals the roasted and tannic notes of cocoa while maintaining great sweetness. A liqueur designed for bartenders seeking the true flavor of chocolate without any coloration. - Gabriel Boudier
Peramangk and Kaurna country. Fresh and crunchy this wine is for all types of fun in the sun. Think peach, nectarine and citrus. Yeahaw!

From Bodbiskhevi in Kakheti region of Georgia. This is from the vaunted producer Pheasant's Tears, produced from the notable Georgian grape variety of rkatsiteli. The wine is produced with extended skin contact in traditional Georgian kvevri vessels. It's got green mango, gingery spice, some earthy, herbal nuance, bright, saline minerality and a good chomp and chew to texture. It delivers a great hit of the variety and the amber winemaking approach. Textbook stuff with pizzazz!

Chewy and chalky, mustard powder in green apple juice with ginger. It’s heady in perfume, bold in flavour, sheets of grippy, crushed rock pucker with gingery, lemon tea notes lingering. Serious wine, very well put together, excellent sense of savouriness and finish. Class. - WineFront.com.au

Elderflower Liqueur is a "must-have" for aperitifs, cocktails based on sparkling wine, white wine, rosé, gin, and vodka, or as a digestif during your festive moments. Perfect for your gourmet pastry recipes, it will perfume your desserts while adding an elegant and refreshing touch. - Gabriel Boudier

In line with tradition, the Peach Liqueur is one of Gabriel Boudier's classics. This fruit liqueur, intense through maceration, offers the illusion of tasting a very juicy and flavourful peach. Derived from maceration, the Vineyard Peach, this springtime and sun-kissed fruit, will delight your taste buds with its slight astringency balanced by fruity and floral aromas. Vineyard Peach Liqueur pleasantly accompanies sparkling wines, dry white wines, sparkling water, and cocktails. It finds its place in desserts, beautifully topping sorbets, and enhances fruit salads. - Gabriel Boudier

Peramangk and Kaurna Country Chilled red. Chilled to the bone. Rose-esque to the eye. This was made with small amounts of everything left in tank that is taking up space, refermented over pinot noir, sauvignon blanc and chardonnay skins. Light and fresh, crunchy textured, rose hip tea and cranberry drink red fruited and dry-chalky. Good sense of vitality here. Easy-pleasing nice and squeezy. Rip in. - WineFront.com.au

Pinechunga plus Peramangk and Kaurna Country A Coonawarra and Adelaide Hills blend. Mostly chardonnay, a small portion of oxidative, solera chardonnay as seasoning. And then also a small amount of sauvignon blanc on top, which is skin fermented. Crisp and refershing, a salty elements, some herbal, cut grass qualities with mixed stone fruit, spicy, pickled ginger and a drizzle of passionfruit. It's frisky and energetic, light on with high drinkability. It's got some pep in its step and a little glide in its stride. Fun. - WineFront.com.au

Peramangk and Kaurna Country Pinot noir and cabernet franc combine their super powers! And also Adelaide Hills and McLaren Vale. A heritage clone of cabernet franc indeed. A kind of bistro red, effortless drinking but interesting, chewy-puckering with tannin, pepper and herbal overlaid on red currants and tart mulberry. Fresh as can be, energetic, ultra crunch through the finish. Pulls up a little short but has all the good times writ large. - WineFront.com.au

Pinechunga Country Coonawarra organic chardonnay. There's an unusual sentence but a good one. Slippery textured, fuller flavoured, crisp edges with a juicy core. Lemon curd, nectarine, light gingery notes, a touch of nougat. It's generous but has a good cut and thrust. Super drinkable, very charming. - WineFront.com.au

wine: Domaine de la Grand-Cour Fleurie Vielles Vignes Le Clos 2023
notes: The Clos de la Grand’Cour situated in the south of the Fleurie appellation, sits on a plateau at around 300m in altitude. The 6,4 hectare parcel, a monopoly of the Dutraive family, lies on fairly deep soils over granite bedrock. This Fleurie cuvée comes from the oldest vines of the parcel, with an average age of 80 years. These vines cover 1,5 hetares of the parcel, and achieved a yield of 18hl/ha in 2022. The grapes were vinified in concrete tanks and the wine was aged in oak barrels for 7 months. - Domaine de la Grand-Cour

wine: Distillerie et Domaines de Provence Absente 55
notes: Absente 55 is enjoyed by those in the know in the true tradition that involves a flame, sugar, water and absinthe… a ceremonial ritual which gives free reign to your imagination. Absente 55 derives its bitterness from several of the aromatic plants of absinthe (Artémisia Absinthium). The Absente 55 recipe, a blend of absinthe, aniseed flavors, mint and spices, gives it its incomparable color and unexpected length of flavor. Tips: Here are a few ideas. Adapt to suit your mood and taste: serve using the traditional spoon method, onto crushed ice or, if you love your drinks strong, just serve it

wine: Domaine de la Grand'Cour Fleurie Lieu-dit Chapelle de Bois 2023
notes: This cuvée comes from vines situated in the “Chapelle des Bois” area (lieu-dit) in the south of the Fleurie appellation. North-west facing, the vines sit at an altitude of between 250 - 300 meters. The sandy topsoil is shallow at the top of the hillside and becomes increasingly deeper towards the bottom, resting on granite bedrock. The 1.8 hectares are planted with thirty-year old vines, producing 20hl/ha for the 2022 vintage. The grapes were vinified in concrete tanks and the wine was aged in 50% in demi-muids and 50% in stainless-steel tanks for 6 months. This thirst-quenching wine can both

Erawirung Country. Made by notable sommelier-turned-wine-importer-turned-winemaker. A man of many hats, Tim Stock. Bright, juicy, summer-time rose vibes, from sangiovese. Think tart raspberry, bright acidity and a lick of cherry and spice.

Zvari is 100% rkatsiteli that sees one week of skin contact and is then aged in tank for nine months and is held in bottle for another year before release. Golden pear, walnut and green tea. Big and juicy, cuddly orchard fruits and the gentlest tug of tannin. Soft acidity, quinine biter refreshment to finish. Clean and bright, a crowd pleaser.

Soif da Vsvam is a collaboration between Pheasant’s Tears and Thierry Puzelat based on 12th Century vine terraces in the southern region of Samtskhe- Javakheti full of volcanic soils and harsh winds, this wine is made from more than 16 ancient Meskhetian varietals from the village of Khertvisi.

Kanz is a whole cluster, carbonic maceration, still red wine that you drink chilled. It is made of Grenache (60%) and Syrah (40%). It is fermented and stored in amphora. Unfined and unfiltered. - Heya Wines

Jaffa Crush is a distinctive Carbonic Still Orange Wine that showcases the unique character of Merwah and Muscat grapes. Made with whole-berry Muscat fermented via carbonic maceration, it is blended over finished direct-press Merwah wine and aged in traditional Amphora. The result is a vibrant, textured wine with a complex interplay of floral aromas, ripe fruit, and subtle tannins, offering a smooth, earthy finish that reflects its ancient winemaking heritage. Perfect for those seeking a bold, natural expression of white wine with a Mediterranean twist. Merwah fermented on skins for 10 days th

The grapes are sourced from a vineyard of 40 year old vines in the commune of Chablis with clay and limestone soils. They were directly-pressed and the juice put in stainless steel tanks where it was fermented and aged on lees for approximately eight months prior to bottling. It is fresh and medium weight, hinting of citrus on the palate, and finishes with energetic freshness and a salty tang. - Living Wines, importer

The grapes for this cuvée are from a vineyard in the commune of Igé, in the Mâconnais, from vines around 55-60 years old. 50% was aged in 400 litre barrels and the rest in stainless steel tanks. The soil is quite deep clay, which makes for a slightly fuller wine, which at first taste is more reminiscent of Chardonnay than Aligoté. - Living Wines, importer

Peramangk and Kaurna Country Half pinots gris and noir. Gris is stomped on and left, then pressed. The pinot noir berries are destemmed into this juice. Then a little press after ten days. A riper year. Scents of dried nectarine, pickled cherry, turned earth and eucalyptus with a little alpine herb character woven through. The palate is hazy in texture, juicy and crisp at once through the finish. Gentle, autumnal characters of leaf, turned earth, field mushrooms with bright, tart red berries underlying. A tonic, a purity, a vivacity. Gastronomic and so digestible. - WineFront.com.au

aromas: Blood Orange, Elderflower, Mushroom, Slate, Saline, Tomato Leaf
notes: Peramangk and Kaurna Country Pinot noir grown on unirrigated, organic farmed vines in a beautiful pocket of the Forest Range parish of the Adelaide Hills. Nature is nurtured on the farm, pasture and vegetable gardens run with the vines, so too native bush and native animal pathways (vines ripped up for it) through the site. No additions at all in the wine, no new oak seasoning, amphora here, a very clear example of seasons follows. Electric wine, scinitillating with saline acidity and general crushed slate minerality. Pumice stone texture on the fringes of juicy, tart cherry, just-ripe mulberr

Peramangk Country. The first release since the 2019 vintage for High Paradise. This exciting and powerful 2023 expression consists of a mixture of early picked fruit, fully ripened fruit and some whole bunch maceration. 2023 High Paradise is a pure expression of Savagnin and Chardonnay from 30+ year old vines. Some Savagnin is crushed by foot along with Chardonnay and then direct pressed and fermented in a favourite old puncheon, whist the other half of the Savagnin ripens for a further week or two. This is then whole bunch macerated, bringing mineral depth, aroma and savouriness to this cuvee

Peramangk and Kaurna country. Aaron Fenwick from a Vine Vale merlot from a vineyard that’s been ‘just farmed’, aka organic farmed since inception. Two day foot stomp on fruit, especially hard on second day, leaning into the Choose Your Own Adventure of is it rose, is it light red, is it chillable, is it room temperature worthy… and bottled without sulphur. Bright and fresh, tart cherry juice, cranberry, sour leaning with peaky, saline and white balsamic-edged acidity, dried flowers, a touch of walnut paste through the finish with a proviso to drink, from my seat, colder and quicker. It’s prett

Peramangk and Kaurna country. Whip Wines is the 'new label' from Aaron Fenwick of Chateau Comme Ci Comme Ca. This one is a merlot. Merlot often can be ho-hum but Aaron is bringing sexy back with merlot. It's a darker fruited expression with choc-cherry, sweet spices, truffle notes and a lick of blood orange. Set to medium weight with plush texture and yet has inherent freshness and uplifting good times vibes. Super easy drinking, plenty of charisma. Sexy indeed.

Peramangk and Kaurna country. A far cry from the tropical, grassy, passionfruit bombs most people associate with our old mate savvy b. This is tart, textural and a subtly oxidative. Savoury-edged with a big hit of saline lemon-lime on the palate, and the inherent racy acidity softened by some time in oak. Drinks almost like some sort of unholy marriage of Loire chenin and Jura savagnin. Unexpected but fun.

Peramangk and Kaurna country. Whole bunches direct pressed to tank for fermentation & racked barrel before the end of primary fermentation. Cellared in barrel for 18 months. Racked to tank one month before bottling in January 2025. Aged in bottle for 12 months before release. Aaron Fenwick, Winemaker

Spritz up as the sun goes down. Sundrift Aperitivo is Brookie's bright and citrus forward aperitif inspired by the golden hour and crafted with native Australian botanicals. It delivers all the bittersweet charm of a classic spritz with more flavour, and a distinctly Byron Bay spirit. Perfect for lazy afternoons, long sunsets, and barefoot gatherings in the sand, Sundrift is your summer in a bottle. Serve simply over ice with prosecco, soda, and a fresh slice of orange for a refreshing and vibrant spritz.

A complex and dry style yuzu liqueur crafted using dried yuzu peels, fresh yuzu peels and whole fresh yuzu fruit. Macerated and distilled in traditional copper pot stills using both pot and vapour infusion techniques. Great for Margaritas, Spritz's, Cosmos and contemporary cocktails. Classic Cocktails... YUZU'D - YUZU'D

Glowing ruby red nuances. Cassis, blueberries, peach skin, resin, humus, pine needles, rhubarb, cinchona, eucalyptus, macerated medicinal herbs, tobacco, and mineral puffs reminiscent of iodine tincture. A generous and crunchy sip, agile yet broad-shouldered, with pleasantly extracted tannins, punctual freshness, and balsamic savoriness. Elegant and persistent. - Iberieli Wine

A small time on skins, so let’s say a yellow rather than orange wine. Has high toned white pepper, cut grass, cucumber in tonic scents with some chinotto and alpine herb gin notes in the mix. The palate is distinct, more dried orange, mustard powder, cumin, some of that white pepper here, but strong, terracotta and sweet earthy elements in play. The finish grippy, pleasingly bitter and juicy-fresh. Proper stuff, and marching to its own beat. - WineFront.com.au

Wurundjeri country. It nods in the direction of Jura with its brine and amontillado scents, a classic line of nashi pear jumps in, toasted, mixed nuts chimes in. What a perfume! Exotic flavours persist too, yes, some pear drop and similar, but mouth-watering saline notes take over, the green almond and hazelnut savouriness runs through, a sizzle through the finish. All this light juiciness bound in feathery, chalky pucker. Just outstanding. Unique too, if that needs to be said. - The Wine Front

wine: Jervis Bay Distilling Co. Bay Aperitivo
notes: Inspired by the Amalfi but made with Australian coastal botanicals, blood oranges, grapefruit & mandarin. This bittersweet Aperitif is vibrant, refreshing, and created for easy and versatile summer drinking. Can be enjoyed as a spritz, in a Negroni, with tonic or simply on the rocks. - Jervis Bay Distilling Co

wine: Bodegas Don Zoilo Amontillado 15 Years Old Sherry
notes: Brilliant hues of old gold and amber. Pungent, intense and complex on the nose, with a subtle note of the fino sherry it had once been and a hint of dried nuts and filberts. Dry, with excellent acidity; a long, full-bodied and elegant palate. A delightfully expressive and unforgettable finish. - Williams & Humbert

Brilliant hues of old gold. Sharply intense and complex aromas reminiscent of the yeast layer, with a note of almond. Very dry on the palate, with a perfect level of acidity. Full-bodied, assertive and elegant with a lingering finish. An extremely expressive and unforgettable wine. - Williams & Humbert

wine: Gabriel Boudier Crème de Violette Liqueur
notes: Gabriel Boudier Violet Liqueur is brimming with sweetness, offering a subtle floral profile. Its delicate taste and color excel in more robust cocktails like a Gin Tonic or as a drizzle over your desserts. For the gourmands, the Violet Liqueur can be enjoyed neat as an aperitif. When paired with dry white wines or Crémants de Bourgogne, it adds a floral, colorful, and indulgent touch. In cuisine, it is ideal as a coulis, finding its place in desserts, and it divinely coats mousses and sorbet. - Gabriel Boudier

Cherry Brandy is the most well-known cherry liqueur. Its uniqueness lies in the blend of different cherry varieties with eau-de-vie. This sweet, flavorful, fruity, and highly aromatic liqueur will enhance all your cocktails. Cherry Brandy Liqueur is very flavorful and can be enjoyed neat over crushed ice, in cocktails, as an aperitif, or even in desserts (as a sauce over fromage blanc). - Gabriel Boudier

Sweet, flavorful, and slightly almond-like, Gabriel Boudier's Apricot Brandy liqueur embodies the house's craftsmanship. It offers you tasting moments rich in the carefully selected flavors of apricot. The Apricot Brandy Liqueur can be enjoyed neat, as a digestif, in cocktails, desserts, and in cooking. Our Apricot Brandy Liqueur pairs well with our Gabriel Boudier vodka in an Apricot Sour cocktail. - Gabriel Boudier

wine: Gabriel Boudier Crème de Cacao Liqueur
notes: Crème de Cacao is one of the delightful and original flavors from Gabriel Boudier. Smooth and with a pronounced cocoa powder finish, it will find its place in all your indulgent recipes. Cacao Liqueur can be enjoyed as an aperitif, in cocktail preparation, or as a digestif. Perfect for a touch of indulgence, it can be used on ice cream, in pastry, or as a coulis on a salad of red fruits. - Gabriel Boudier

wine: Gabriel Boudier Crème de Mures Wild Blackberry Liqueur
notes: The Blackberry Liqueur is one of Gabriel Boudier's classics, with its aromatic density and distinctive notes making it rich in flavor. This liqueur captures the finesse and sweetness of the fruit, along with slightly herbaceous and musky notes typical of blackberries. The Blackberry Liqueur is perfect for an aperitif with dry white wine, crémant, or in your cocktail recipes. Ideal as a coulis, it finds its place in desserts, beautifully topping mousses and sorbets. - Gabriel Boudier

Be transported to the Mediterranean with our signature Limoncello. Made from our family’s time-honoured recipe, it’s crafted for meaningful moments and good company. Serve it ice-cold as a crisp digestif, mix it into a refreshing spritz, or drizzle over desserts for a citrusy twist. However you pour it, this is la dolce vita in a bottle. - Solbevi

Only two Chartreuse monks know the identity of the 130 plants, how to blend them and how to distill them, they are also the only ones who know which plants they have to macerate to produce the natural green and yellow colours. Herbaceous and fresh vegetal flavours are most dominate, the complex flavours include lemon zest, mint, pine ad aniseed. Drink cold or over ice. Don't leave it at the back of the liquor cabinet like our parents did!

Taungurung Country From up in the Vic high country, cool site, ups and downs in the landscape, green hills, rocky outcrops and prosecco through that all. This is straight up and down, a little x-factor in its coursing minerality, very refreshing. It's made with a good time in mind, and making the variety and style a bit more interesting, just that little kinky. Yeah!

The Radice Amaro is a root-based amaro. It is made from fresh bergamot, the roots of angelica, licorice, ukogi, and chicory. Also with an addition of the legendary herb "black cumin" that was discovered on a trip to Hong Kong as the final piece to complete the drink. More than 30 types of botanicals are used, and a miraculous yellow (root) amaro was completed. This is a limited production item and is bottled with a cork stopper. There may be sediment on rare occasions, this is hand-bottled product thus filtration is minimal to keep the character of the drink intact. - Black Market Sake Founded

Founded in 2021 by distiller Tatsuya Motonaga, Iseya Distillery resides in a repurposed traditional house that's more than 100 years old. Having worked in some of the world's most recognised cocktail bars (Shinjuku's Ben Fiddich, Shibuya's Coal Ila and Taipei's Wa-shu) Motonaga got the amaro bug after a huge distillery tour of Europe and the UK. He was hooked by the level of craftmanship, connection to local agriculture that create this drink of epic folkloric proportions. And how lucky are we to now have a Japanese interpretation Aperitivo is the first regular bottling from Iseya Distillery.

wine: Alessandro Stefani La Veduta Pinot Noir 2024
notes: Wurundjeri country. Stacks of character, silky texture, a little grip, huge perfume of sour cherry, old rose petals, Autumn leaves, nori, salted liquorice. The same to taste, but fruity, dark, soft, some gravelly edges, white mushroom to finish. Sweet, dry, rose hip tea rolls in too. Succulent, cool, light, fine. A beautiful, savoury pinot noir of distinction. Just so damn good. - The Wine Front

Wurundjeri country. Old clone, taken from grandpa’s vineyard in Tuscany, is the story. Chewy, brooding, cola and char, ripe plums, mulberry, blueberry and smoky paprika spice. It’s a sloshy texture with a few ribs of chalky tannin, long lived in flavour, gently spicy and oyster saucy to finish. Nice feel to this, easy to drink, a more robust rendering of the variety, but well balanced and full of charm. - The Wine Front

35% Chardonnay, 35% Welschriesling, 20% Viognier, 5% Petit Manseng, 3% Gewürztraminer, 2% Muscat Blanc from Ningxia. Fermented with indigenous yeasts. MLF encouraged with aging in old oak for 8 months. Small portion of 2022 Yunnan Chardonnay added for lift. Dried orange peel, kumquat, Oolong tea on the nose, with a floral jasmine- lychee lift.- Periphery Wines, Importer Ian Dai, sommelier-turned-winemaker, educator, global wanderer and the brains and brawn behind the cult-like Xiao Pu wines. His fingerprints are all over a range of expressive, creative, distinct and intriguing wines . The wine

51% Syrah, 25% Pinot Noir, 10% Chardonnay, 5% Welschriesling, 5% Muscat Hamburg, 2% Marselan, 2% Dunkelfelder from Ningxia. Bottled in 2025. Dense dark and red fruit, but also a firm thread of soy and mushroom umami that runs through the core of cherry, black plums, chestnuts, and star anise. - Periphery Wines, Importer Ian Dai, sommelier-turned-winemaker, educator, global wanderer and the brains and brawn behind the cult-like Xiao Pu wines. His fingerprints are all over a range of expressive, creative, distinct and intriguing wines . The wines speak authentically of their varied regions, uniq

wine: Curatif X Bar Bambi: Amaretto Sour
notes: Who can resist an Amaretto Sour? You know you want to...
Tags: Food, Things To Eat
Honestly ... these are the best chips of all time, just treat yourself. WHO DOESN'T LOVE COMTÉ?! We eat these while drinking wines from Jura. Outstanding!
Bring the classic flavour of French fries with sauce to your snack time with Brets Pommes Frites Sauce chips! Chip flavoured chips!

This smooth tasting delight proudly hold the title of our most popular relish. A simple get together of tomatoes balanced with a careful selection of spices. It's all natural and it's perfect on everything. - Women's Work Ingredients: Ripe Tomato (51%), vinegar, onion, sugar, cornflour, spices, salt

wine: Women's Work Spicy Green Tomato Relish 330g
notes: A resurrected master recipe passed down from great-granny Ida (and her grandma too). M ore savoury than our Ripe Tomato Relish with some sweet and sour notes . We are fussy about all the fruit we buy, but we like our green tomatoes to be quite hard and dark green so that they not only give us the slight tartness that we like, but also a good, firm texture. - Women's Work Ingredients: Green Tomato (51%), vinegar, onion, sugar, cornflour, spices, salt

This Lemon Pepper Relish is a taste of its own. It takes us far beyond the bitter sweet of a marmalade to a world of flavours that challenge and tantalise the palate at the same time - sweet, bitter, sour, umami, salty – all 5 basic tastes. Add black peppercorns hand-ground in mortar and pestle and you have a match made in heaven. The peppercorns are not evenly ground so that even though there is an even distribution of peppery flavour there are crunchy pieces of peppers and sometimes the odd whole corn to bight on. It is delicious. Ingredients: Lemon (42%), vinegar, onion, sugar, pepper (1.3%

Granny's have been making beetroot relish since Adam was a boy and we totally get why, it preserves beautifully, grows in abundance and its so so pretty. That colour! And it’s all natural! Our beetroot relish has only a few ingredients, but it only needs a few things to set off the naturally sweet, earthiness of the beetroot. - Women's Work Ingredients: Beetroot (49%), vinegar, onion, apple, sugar, spice

For this delightful creation we have women to thank. Many have worked away at this recipe, making one small improvement at a time with each passing of hands. From us we add a touch of chilli and use local, earth grown ingredients, just a touch of sugar and absolutely no BS. Expect a rich tomato flavour with a pinch of chilli to finish. - Women's Work Ingredients: Ripe Tomato (51%), vinegar, onion, sugar, cornflour, spices, chilli, salt
The classic, with a wicked streak. Cola spiced with clove, cassia, cardamom and nutmeg, finished with vanilla and kola nut.
Bright, sharp and ready to tell all. Real lemon juice meets fragrant yuzu, and nobody keeps a secret.
Sweet blood orange juice up front, then a ginger kick and a hint of juniper on the way out. Bittersweet and refreshing.

Spanish pickled chillies. Delicious. The best! Cook with them, chuck them in a sandwich, add them to a charcuterie board or just gobble them straight from the jar, late at night, illuminated only by the light of your refrigerator, like some sort of feral little snack goblin. We won't judge.

wine: Death Of A Classic Grand Single Barrel Chardonnay 2025
aromas: Peach, Apricot, Lemon, Ginger, Vanilla, Honey, Butter
notes: Wonnarua Country From a single site. Aged on lees in barrel. Wild ferment. This isn’t shy. It’s ripe peach and honey-lemon-ginger tea with some sizzled butter, vanilla cream and sweet citrus trough lolly scents. The palate a similarity, oily textured with meaty stone fruit, dried coconut apricot, more sizzled butter and a lick of preserved lemon. There’s a chubbiness to the wine, a slow moving feel and gently palate staining too. Time will deliver more richness and roundness, one can tell, and pleasingly so. - WineFront.com.au

wine: Death Of A Classic Amphora Aged Semillon 2025
notes: Wonnarua Country This wine sees 12 hours skin contact, a press, then six months maturation in amphora on lees. Golden-ish, bright colour. Waxy texture, quite the depth and richness here yet a cooling, saline core elevating things. Grilled lime, spicy, crystallised ginger, faint toffee apple notes, not quite sweet but has a ripe-ish fruit profile and a slip and slide to texture unlike most Hunter semillon. Good extension of flavour, a little diffuse in the personality stakes, but way interesting all up and fun. - WineFront.com.au

Taungurung Country There’s no denying the richness and concentration in this wine. And the length. In fact, this wine has a long finish as a starting point. It’s a loop, really. First sip, long finish, next sip. And on we go. Apples, peaches, cashews and toasted oats. This is a pretty solid base and the definition of this wine. Plenty of fruit, but with no tropical sunshine here, sweetness of ripeness—yes, but very much a savoury drive and a dry tail end. Then comes the sprinkle, the topping, the cherry on top—apple tart, custard powder, milk bottle lolly, cinnamon. Yes, all things we love and
Tags: France, Jura, Savagnin, Vin Jaune

The grapes for this négoce cuvée are from the hallowed Cote d’Or village of Volnay, from Mercurey further south, and, closer to the Montanets’ home, from Vézelay in the north. Each source was vinified separately. In each case whole bunches were macerated in tank. They did regular punch downs, each time going deeper until eventually the remaining grapes are “swimming” as Valentin Montanet puts it. Before it is too cold it was pressed then returned to tank to finish fermentation. Once it was finished fermenting the Volnay was aged in 400 litre barrels and the Mercurey and Vézelay juice in foudre

Mouth-watering melon from Burgundy! Harvested from 30 year old vines, certified organic and aged in stainless steel for up to 10 months, this is one of those glittery, beautiful wines that will linger in your memory forever. Mineral driven, juicy pear, white florals and green apple, w e'd pair this exceptional wine with terrines, parfaits, and / or charcuterie.

Anara began in the heart of a home filled with the scent of masala chai. Charlotte Priya, Australian born with Indian roots, grew up steeped in the tradition of her Nani’s renowned spiced tea. A single jar was left of Nani’s masala chai following her departure from this earth. Many in the family tried to recreate it and failed. The last brew of this tea was sipped and the era came to an end. — Anara is an homage to Nani — A masala chai liqueur born from her story and handcrafted after years of refining by Charlotte and her partner Swan on the South Coast of Australia.
