wine: Worlds Apart Wines Rites Of Spring Grenache 2024
notes: Peramangk Country From grenache vines planted in deep ancient sand in 1958 and lovingly tended by Fiona Wood. This is a lighter style of grenache with fine detailed tannins from judicious whole bunch fermentation. The name refers to a Washington DC post-hardcore band, which in turn was referring to a Stravinsky ballet that caused a full blown riot in Paris, which in turn was referring to ancient Pagan rituals in which a “Chosen One” was sacrificed to the Earth by dancing until their death… - Worlds Apart

wine: Worlds Apart Wines Hope Forest Sauvignon Blanc 2025
notes: Peramangk and Kaurna Country. Adelaide Hills Sauvignon Blanc but not as you know it: mature vines, excellent viticulture and a cold site, combined with wild barrel fermentation make for a crisp and fresh but full bodied wine that displays aromas and flavours of ripe white peach and melon and a long, dry and full bodied palate. - Louis and Hannah, wine makers

Peramangk Country A warm summer and an early harvest, offset by a cold, elevated vineyard has made for a chardonnay of refined elegance, with underlying powerful flavour and layers of complexity. The vineyard is in the heart of the Piccadilly Valley, grown by the Virgara family. Clones are 76 and 96. This is an elegant and fresh but complex chardonnay that we're very proud of. Drinking window 2026-2036. - Louis Schofield, wine maker

Noongar Country. White grapes, fresh as, from Frankland River. Around a week or so on skins and then blended with a splash of fresh white wine juice to perk things up. Zesty, tart and very refreshing. Electric and sour-leaning with citrus and green herb characters in spades. A crunch of green apple too, a chalky, puckering finish. Yew!

Kaurna & Peramangk Country A blend of shiraz and grenache with a splash of chenin blanc for extra pizzazz! Slurpy red cherry and blackberry, plum skin and herbal tones. But what makes this even more delicious, is that is was named in honour of an event our good friend Taras Ochota put on many moons ago. Grab your sequin onesie out of the back of the wardrobe, play some Donna Summer and pour yourself a large goblet and don't look back!!

Jirawirung Country Lovers of this variety in France, we were looking to produce something fresh and elegant but still true to its personality and something a little richer in our range of whites. Notes of ripe banana and yellow tropical fruit expression complimented by delicate oak spice aromas. Tick! The palate echos the banana fruit with super ripe sweet yellow peach. The concentrated flavours reach down the back of the throat. And the texture? Silky and slippery; a softness that makes the fruit seem even richer but freshness is always maintained. Tim Stock, wine maker

wine: Domaine Alzitella Ile de Beaute Blanc 2023
notes: Vermentino from France's Île de Beauté appelation, aka the island of Corsica. Crunchy seaside Mediterranean white vibes through and through on this one. Someone pass me an oyster immediately!

Peramangk Country A return to 100% sauvignon blanc this year. Two parcels – Lansdowne at Forreston in the northern part of the Hills and Magpie Springs at the far southern end. Lovely yellow gold with orange tones and a light haze to denote its time with skins (and lack of filtration or fining!). This time expect aromas of persimmon, dried mango, mandarin, jalapeno, ginger spice, peach iced tea and dried herbs. The palate is rich and textural with ripe persimmon, orange rind and spice with juicy mineral toned acid and fine tea-like tannins for texture. Another delicious variation on the same t

Peramangk Country The winemaker just quipped to us 'Collines, you know that's hills in French?', and we nodded sagely... This comes from the Adelaide Hills, maybe a clue, but we shan't be so literal. Non! This is a stunning pinot, light weight but flavoursome, cinched with fine, sandy tannins, sits on the cusp of ripe cherry fruitiness with a splash of mushroomy earthiness in the mix. Pretty, delicious. Pretty delicious. Go on.

Tinta barocca, syrah, and then bits of grenache, cinsault and 1% carignan for x-factor. Screw capped. Organic vines and a solid expression of Swartland’s new age, though we’re over a decade past that original conversation. Supple and rich, layered with woody and herbal spice, wonderfully loose knit and yet with some depth, brooding, darker fruits and nutty-woody characters. Mellow, wildly appealing, a faint wild edge of tang and freshness too. Such ease of drinking and easy appeal – albeit this is a more wintery, cooler night red wine. - The Wine Front

Peramangk Country. A Grenache forward blend with Pinot Noir and Syrah. The nose is a spellbinding mix of bright candied red berry fruits, violets, and spice. The palate opens up to pomegranate, cinnamon, and a lemon tart finish. Crunchy and light yet complex and multifaceted wine. Drinks well chilled. - Edenflo

grapes: Pinot Noir, Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, Shiraz
notes: Peramangk, Ngadjuri, and Kaurna Country. "Syrah/cabernet. 60/40. New World – new millennium claret. Deep alluring colour. Lifted, blackcurrant, black plum, bramble, pepper and clove on the nose. Medium bodied, juicy and balanced, black and blue fruits juicy so drinkable." – Edenflo

Peramangk, Ngadjuri, and Kaurna Country. The 2022 Chuck Berry is a vibrant Grenache-Syrah blend that reimagines a classic with contemporary flair. Bright raspberry and bramble fruit notes are beautifully balanced by earthy undertones and savoury spice, creating a wine with real depth and character.

wine: Yayoi Wines Mon Grand Frère Cabernet Franc 2024
notes: Dja Dja Wurrung Country “My big brother” The more opulent counterpart to “Fèrot” my other cabernet franc, this wine was made to with intention and precision Sourced from the iconic Ex Virgin Hill block at Glenhope Vineyard planted in 1995 on granite, volcanic, and sandy loam soils, it is a wine that speaks clearly of site, season. Undergoing wild yeast fermentation, the wine was gently extracted over a long, slow maceration spending 21 days on skins before being pressed to barrel. It was then matured for 13 months in seasoned oak, allowing the wine to evolve with purity. - Yayoi Wines From Gle

wine: Yayoi Wines Rose of Two Thorns 2024
aromas: Cranberry, Pomegranate, Grapefruit, Blood Orange, Almond
notes: Kaurna Country "This I call chenin rouge“, offers winemaker Steffi Snook, ‘pineau d’aunis, often jokingly called chenin rouge, can be made into rosé in Loire so I wanted to emulate those deeper style rosé wines of Anjou”. After initial chenin and cabernet franc ferments kick off, the wine finishes by co-fermenting – the sum of parts, hence, of Loire’s fabled white and red variety. So Cabernet Chenin Blanc Franc, perhaps. A vibrant, garnet coloured wine. Lush texture, a little shimmy of rich glossiness, staining the palate gently, a finish that corkscrews with blood orange and pink grapefruit j

Woiwurrung Country. Raised along the eastern edge of Gunnings Sugarloaf in Tasmania's sheltered upper Coal River Valley. This powerful cuvée benefits from 100% whole cluster inclusion lending spice and intense graphite to the crushed black fruit core.- Mise En Place

wine: Mise En Place Le Jardin Grenache 2026
notes: Woiwurrung Country. Grown on an organic site in the sun-burnt rolling hills of the Pyrenees in Western Victoria. This destemmed fruit received delicate handling and underwent a long cold soak period before a short maceration on skins to capture the pretty aromatics so crucial for this chillable style.- Mise En Place

Yorta Yorta Country. Single hectare site, organically farmed - a hard find in the Yarra Valley. 12 months sur lie lends a refined plush texture which is balanced by sturdy acidity & concentrated golden green fruit and fennel seeds aromatics.- Mise En Place

wine: Mise En Place Le Jardin Riesling 2026
notes: Yorta Yorta Country. Hand harvested from an organic site in the quartz-riddled hills of the Pyrenees. This fruit was then treated with a delicate hand, wholecluster pressed and fermented in stainless steel using native yeast to preserve its delicate floral aromatics and lively acid line.- Mise En Place

aromas: Raspberry, Blood Orange, White Pepper, Hazelnut, Beeswax
notes: A GSM from Tavel, carbonic maceration, off to older oak barrique. Almost a beeswax, floral note over the wild raspberry, brambly red currant characters, white pepper and faint game meat - inviting perfume. Supple in the palate, a touch plush even, raspberry liquorice, some candied nuts and dried mixed peel, blood orange through the finish with some silty pucker. A bit of hazelnut and wild herb to finish. - The Wine Front

Go go grenache. Maybe some cinsault. Carbonic macerated for 12 days or so. Tank and old barrique. Purple-garnet colour. A grand release, jubey blackcurrant fruit meets grippy, stoney tannin, cassis and smoky black tea, white pepper. Slurpy and then serious, a pumice stone texture to finish. And yet juicy. Crikey. What a drink here! Serious and fun in the same gobful. - The Wine Front

Grenache, cinsault, carignan. Plugged into the electricity socket colour. Energised by the perfume, red cherry, rose petals, spice and alpine herbs. Floral lift. It's a ripper. The palate succulent, pippy, mineral charged and stony with fine, minerally tannin. Such vivid, fresh, red berry and plummy fruit flavours with sage leaf and tarragon leafy notes throughout. So delightful, so well done. - The Wine Front

Grenache, carignan and maybe some clairette makes its way in. Matured in big barrels. Cloudy rose mode. Orange garnet amber colour. The perfume is quiet and red fruited, rose hip on the bush and green almond. The palate drinks more like a textural white wine, slippery, rich, but with light grip shaping things nicely. Touches of green tea leaf in that rose hip tea too. Savoury times. Good. - The Wine Front

All roussanne, all day. Direct pressed, to older oak barrels, on lees. Slippery texture with a swish of Brazil nut, preserved lemon, a delightful bitter edge with plushness but not richness, and still a kind of cool finish. Spice, grapefruit, curls of soft tannin in a way. A distinct, Southern Rhone white wine but with freshness, despite volume. Palate staining. Great drink. - The Wine Front

wine: Romain le Bars Le Clau Blanc 2025
notes: Ugni blanc, picked at more mature fruit character, with acid retained. Old oak. Rested on lees. No added anything. Salted peanuts, some wakame seaweed notes, ginger, lemon curd, apple tea with cinnamon but cool. Hazy texture, richness but cool and chiseled edges. Nuttiness sweeps through gently, finishes the wine savoury but a very fine briny finish counters well. A gastronomic wine. Impressive. - The Wine Front

wine: Romain le Bars Ancestral Petillant Naturel 2024
notes: Methode Ancestrale and made from ugni blanc, roussanne. From the family estate. Attractive scents of just ripe stone fruit, green mango, some sea spray elements, hay and straw, green peppercorn and some fir and pine needle. Creamy texture, guava notes, curiously, marzipan, pickled ginger, very tea-like elements to the wine - exotic and delicious. Soft bubbles, cool acidity to finish. - The Wine Front

producer: Frankly This Wine was Made By Bob
grapes: Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Gris, Marsanne
notes: Ngurra Country. Each year the ‘Blanc’ has been released, by the father-son winemaking duo of the Colmans, the wine shape shifts based on ‘best of’ white varieties of the season. The wine is always interesting in its mesh of various fruit characters, from tropical through to citrus, with floral lift, racy mineral qualities and nutty savouriness. Layers on layers. All this and it remains in a somewhat lightweight frame too. Vibrancy plus!

Taungurung Country Our delicious Nebbiolo Rosé, Ada, is back! This wine offers an elegant texture and mouthfeel, with aromas of strawberry, orange peel, and white blossom. On the palate, its crisp acidity brings a truly refreshing finish. Made from 100% nebbiolo grapes, this rosé began her journey amongst the honey hued trees of the high country. From there, she was pressed off skins, before fermenting and ageing on fine lees in neutral French oak over the winter, arriving here to make your acquaintance today. - Foreign Friends
Locally hand made Maltese sourdough crackers loaded with garlic, onion and sesame and poppy seeds - perfect for all cheese and drips.

Wiradjuri and Ngunnawal Country This one gets a ferment on its skins for three weeks, and is then aged in amphora for seven months. It ends up in this slick and grippy textural zone, still balistically refreshing but dialling in lighter characters of orange wines, while still being one! Go figure! Good scents and flavours of nashi pear, green pineapple, pickled ginger and preserved lemon. Summery fun, warm weather skin ferment wine personified. - WineFront.com.au

Wiradjuri and Ngunnawal Country Whoowee, this is a live one. A pitch perfect chillable red? A crunchy, frisky (just shy of medium weight) barbera for late night? A vibrant expression of the variety regardless and does a great trick of showing off the variety's best assets in fresh, red cherry brightness, a slosh of wild raspberry, a good dusting of woody and herbal spices, a crisp texture and a long, refreshing finish. Gosh, this is a great drink. - WineFront.com.au

Wiradjuri and Ngunnawal Country A blend of mostly aleatico with some chenin blanc to lend interest and character. Interest and character indeed. An electric pulse through this wine, lightning bolts of tart cherry, rose hip tea and blood orange twang. Super refreshing, almost Campari meets vermouth kinda vibes, but still with the attractive, Italian-esque rose/rosato vibes going on. Thirst crusher of the highest order. - WineFront.com.au

A famed French aperitif liqueur Suze was created in 1889, at the Rousseau, Laurens and Moureaux distillery in the outskirts of Paris. Flavoured with Gentian Root (which is still sourced from Jura to this day), this bitter sweet aperitif has with a spicy fruitiness to it. Suze can be consumed neat or on ice, but can also be used as the bitter component for many cocktails.

wine: Sông Cái Distillery Bong Bóng Sparkling Yellow Rice Wine 2025
notes: Bong Bóng means bubbly. A perpetual reserve blend of rice wines aged up to 4 years in oak and terracotta amphora. 100% nép Cáí Hao Váng (Yellow Flower sticky rice). Fermented with native microbes. Nutty, bubbly and fun.

wine: Sông Cái Distillery Tung Tóe Purple Rice Wine Pet Nat 2025
notes: Tung Tóe is a vibe. The energy, excitement and eruption that comes with the HISS and POP of a bottle of bubbly wine. 100% nép cám (Black or Purple sticky rice). Notes of baked bread, tropical flowers and tart dark berries.

wine: Mullineux Kloof Street Swartland Chenin Blanc 2024
notes: Our Kloof Street range is all about freshness, balance and great drinkability. Grapes for our Kloof Street Chenin Blanc come from vineyard parcels on a variety of soils in different parts of the Swartland. The wine is part tank and part barrel fermented. Pale straw in colour, this wine has a nose of sun ripened pears and wet granite. The palate has a vibrant acidity balanced by a soft, round texture and some pithy character. The wine has a fresh, mineral finish. - Mullineux Wines
A classic cocktail garnish for a reason!

Pronounced CO-KEY, Cocchi Americano Bianco Aperitivo has been produed in the same way since 1891 when it was first made by pastry chef Giulio Cocchi. Made in the style of of bianco vermouth from moscato d’asti, it is fortified with brandy and aromatised with botanicals which include gentian and cinchona bark, along with orange peels and herbs (the full recipe is a secrete). Soft and round it is perfect for drinking as an aperitif on ice with a twist of orange or in classic cocktails such as Vespa Martini and a Corpse Reviver #2.

Pronounced CO-KEY, Cocchi Americano rosa uses the two aromatic varietals bracheotto and malvasia from Italy's Piedmont region before being fortified and aromatised with gentian, cinchona, citrus zest, ginger and rose petal. Serve with soda over ice or gussy your next glass of prosecco up with a few dashes.
Tags: Mixer, Soft Drink

wine: Autonomy Distillers Australian Davo Plum Aperitivo Bitter
notes: Tart Davidson Plum and Rosella are balanced by sweet Aussie oranges and a hint of Tasmanian Pepperberry. Add a splash of soda for an easy Aussie spritz, or combine with a generous pour of sparkling wine and plenty of ice for a cool cocktail that will see you through a hot summer arvo. - Autonomy Distillery

Husband and wife team Felix and Corinna set out to make 'bloody good booze' and our word they have! One of our favourite spirits that has been released this year, we can't get enough! The team say it sits somewhere between Campari and Aperol, but we say it’s worlds better than both, with a proper sense of bitterness and lots of native Australian character care of rosella, Davidson’s plum and anise myrtle. Over rocks or in a Negroni bam she hits the spot!

Permangk Country. Made by notable sommelier-turned-wine-importer-turned-winemaker. A man of many hats, Tim Stock. This is a decidedly lighter red wine expression, intentionally. Slurpy, aromatic, fresh-feeling red. Delicious. Sour cherry, graphite minerality, dried green herbs, a bit of black pepper. Flavoursome and yet super refreshing. Enough meat on bones too. A delight to drink, and typifying what Aussie reds should look like in a summery-to-autumnal context.

peramangk Country Ah the PIG as this variety is affectionately known inside the winery. A blend of around 60% barrel fermented and 40% tank, all on gross lees until bottling. Sourced from the certified organic Lansdowne Vineyard. Soft pale straw colour. The nose has good intensity but as desired has a kind of fruit neutrality like the best northern Italian examples. That said you can see the fresh pear and apple notes along with dried white and yellow flowers and a hint of dairy thanks to the lees aging in the barrel component. The palate is really where the style diverges from commercial exam
Pinot blanc, sylvaner, riesling and gewurztraminer. Alsace

Muller thurgau, gruner veltliner, welschriesling. Czech one litre magic. Blended for your pleasure. Has that lovely aroma of warm, lemon-honey-ginger tea and faint tropical fruits. Pretty start. Juicy in the palate with a clatter of tropical fruits, frisky-fresh saline acidity with ultra-refreshing feel. Relatively simple but an utter delight to drink. Summery white personified, with tension and tang on its side. - The Wine Front

wine: Viamic Etern Vi Blanc Metode Naturale 2024
notes: In wine and friendship, nothing is as important as what they bring us. The 'viamic' claims a subjective perception of the world and wine. A project that was born from the desire to break barriers between wine and people and that wants to allow links to be established in an organic way, with freedom of interpretation and enjoyment. A space to dialogue and imagine among friends where 4G will never be able to reach. A white wine made with macabeu grapes that come from Font-Rubí in Alt Penedès. Accessible, vibrant and bright. - Jaume Jorda, producer

Jubey red fruits and freshness, light and easy drinking with an array of food and an absolute crowd pleaser. In the warmer months it even happily enjoys a chill in the fridge. The Swiss Army Knife of the wine world!

Taungurung Country Medium bodied with red fruits including red currents and satsuma plum, savoury and sweet spices, a lovely cola note from the Tempranillo, delicate tannins, good acid drive and amazing length. A fantastic red for any season. - Municipal Wines

Taungurung Country. Two day cold soak, followed by fermentation on skins of between 8 and 20 days to build complexity, gentle punch-downs twice a day to extract the amazing character of the thick skins without extracting too much tannin, before being pressed off into barrel for a total of 37 days of fermentation with lees stirring twice weekly to increase complexity and mouthfeel. Following fermentation the wine was moved to tank to retain freshness and those wonderful citrus and floral aromas. Bottled unfined and unfiltered. - Municipal Wines

wine: Municipal Wines Skin Contact Pinot Gris 2022
aromas: Strawberry, Red Apple, Rose Petal, Almond
notes: Taungurung Country Delicate and super complex with red apple skin, rose petal, strawberry, hints of almond and a lovely note of sweet spice. With great acid drive and wonderful length and freshness. - Municipal Wines

Ngunnawal Country Sassafras perplexes us at P&V year in and year out, to how they also manage to be so consistent in the pet nat department. One of the hardest wine styles to be consistent in due to the unpredictable nature of any fermentation during it's main ferment. Unlike a lot of pet nats, this one seems to have a perfect balance of richness and creaminess but still have an intense acidic backbone. Every time we open this bottle, it's always a fight for the last glass!

Kambuwal Country. 90% Verdelho from the Robert Channon Vineyard in Amiens and 10% Viognier from St Judes Vineyard Ballandean, Granite Belt, QLD. The Verdelho was wild fermented as whole berries with twice daily pump overs for the first 7 days. Warm ferments without being hot to aid extraction. We then moved to hand plunging for the second week before being pressed after 15 days. It was then pressed long and slow to tank for settling. The Viognier was pressed immediately but pumped straight over lightly pressed Verdelho skins, as we much prefer the structure achieved macerating on Verdelho. It

Wonnarua Country. Lots of flavour and personality, waxy lime, cumquat, thick ginger notes, some honey-glazed cashew nut, cinnamon, lemon verbena, lime pickle. A feast for the senses. It’s medium weight and yet finds cut and shards of crisp acidity. There’s layers to the personality of the wine. It’s got intensity and flow and freshness. It’s got some potency of honey and caramel and toffee too. Flavourtown. Fun. Complex. Excellent drinking. - The Wine Front

Noongar Country. This is a new wine intended as a partner for Small Town with a similar smashable vibe. Gewurztraminer, Pinot Gris and Riesling. A bit of skin contact, a bit of co-fermentation, 6 months on lees. Jasmin flower, Pink grapefruit, guava and lychee. Fire up the De Lorean, ride a rainbow to a Pystopian future! - Brave New Wine

wine: Perello Cocktail Picante Olives and Pickles
notes: Pitted green Manzanilla olives and black Cuquillo olives with stones, combined with pickled silverskin onions and baby gherkins in a spicy marinade spiked with pickled guindilla chillis. The perfect combination for the lover of pickles and olives.

If you know, you know..... For those friends who don't know, t he Manzanilla olive, a quintessential Spanish, Perello olives are packed with hot guindilla green peppers and marinated in Manzanilla. Pop 'em in your cooking, pop 'em on a charcuterie or cheese board, pop 'em in your martini, just pop 'em in your mouth!

wine: Champagne Francis Orban Extra Brut NV
notes: The Extra-Brut cuvée is a champagne with the balance and freshness of juicy fruit. It is perfect for drinking with friends or as an aperitif and can be enjoyed right through to when you serve your sweeter culinary inspirations. - Champagne Francis Orban 100% pinot meunier

grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, Shiraz, Cabernet Franc
notes: Wizard Piss is the brainchild of Sam Leyshon from Mallaluka in Yass, NSW with the original wine one that stood out from Sam’s usual roster of wines and labelled for its more alternative styling. I t's basically a blend of mataro (60%), cabernet sauvignon (30%) and shiraz (10%) from our home block in Yass. Medium weight, earthy and dark fruit characters, dried Italian herbs, a bit of goji berry and a splash of blood orange. And naturally a splash of hocus pocus for good measure!

Lutruwita Country Kevin is a release from the Brian wine trio of Peter Dredge (Dr Edge), Joe Holyman (Stoney Rise/Holyman) and our Mike Bennie. Kevin wines are wines that sit outside the usual trio of releases from Brian, born from additional creativity and interest in unusual blends. Oh, and instead of 375ml, Kevin is in 750ml bottles... Here we have a blend of riesling and semillon. Not uncharted territory in terms of blends that may have occurred before, but from Tasmania, perhaps a first. This is textural in that beautifully chalky, puckering way, super bright in acidity, very refreshing,
Kaurna Country. Grenache rose from Blewitt Springs in McLaren Vale. Very pale. Very dry. Very refreshing. Think Provence without the price tag!

wine: CO-OP Wines Yarra Valley Pinot Noir 2025
notes: Woiwurrung Country. A collaborative project from neighbouring Yarra Valley winemakers Alessandro Stefani and Doug Lilburne of Mise En Place wines, using fruit from the Stefani family's vineyards. Bright, fresh, easy-going pinot noir. Red fruited with a smattering of dried herbs in the background, a backbone of crunchy acidity and fine chalky tannins to finish. Absolutely wouldn't hate half an hour in the fridge before cracking it.

wine: Proper Crisps Big Cut Dill Pickle
notes: Don't be a dill. Dive in!! This is going to be dill-icious! Enjoy the zingy tang of Apple Cider Vinegar with a subtle hint of pickling herbs and Dill. Sure to get your tastebuds dancing. Made using 100% New Zealand grown potatoes, High Oleic Sunflower Oil and a sprinkle of Marlborough Sea Salt. Hand-cooked in small batches by our 'Proper Chefs' who make sure only the best, most golden crisps end up in each bag! You can really taste the difference. Once the last morsel has been devoured, simply pop the packet in your garden compost and it will naturally decompose – how eco is that! - Proper Cri
Great Uncle Kenny's Amazing SnackaChangi Chips! Chunky, Crunchy, Crispy, Brass Kettle Fried, Corrugated Chips! "They said it couldn't be done, but we put the Vinegar in first!"

aromas: Cranberry, Pomegranate, Blood Orange, Sea Spray
notes: Taungurung Country How about some tasting notes from the Pool Wines winemakers? Looks like a glowing ruby gemstone in the glass. Pomegranate, white plums and crunchy red apples. Energetic and fresh, and a well incorporated volatility lift to brighten it up even further. From us? Frisky red, cranberry drink meets wild herbs with a dash of uplifting sea spray and zesty, blood orange twang. Sounds fruit, edgy, cool. It is. Get in. Drink chilled.

The tag team trio of dreams, Bennie, Dredge and Holyman bring you a pinot gris fermented for a long time on skins. It's somewhere between a cloudy strawberry rosé/orange wine/super bright light fresh red even, has a sunset pink/purple hue, loads of tannin and texture, feels refreshing, makes you amazing. Whatever you want it to be. Warning : dangerously moreish.

Lutruwita Country. Dr Edge 'Brut Nature' is a Traditional Method Sparkling blend of Tamar Valley Pinot Noir, Chardonnay & Pinot Meunier. Predominantly 2022 and 2021 base material, the wine is left to develop in bottle on tirage for 2 years. - Disgorged 'Brut Nature' or 'Bone Dry' - July 2024. - Dr Edge Whoa. A zero dosage and zero sulphur Brut Nature. What gives? It comes crown sealed for your pleasure and ease of drinking but is way, way more complex than you think. And yet so effortless and cool, frisky and energetic, lots of minerally detail, hazy apple juice, some faint nuttiness, a lick o

wine: Champagne Andre Jacquart Vertus Experience Blanc de Blanc NV
notes: Serious stuff here from a fourth and fifth-generation family-owned grower domaine specialising in Chardonnay. Intense freshly baked bread and toasty, savoury aromas with subtle oak complemented by a sprightly freshness. Extended lees contact adds a lovely fermented dimension and makes for splendid bubbles. The perfect apéritif.

A blend of Premier Cru chardonnay, pinot noir and pinot meunier from the Montagne de Reims district of Champagne. This sub-region is famed for it's fine, chalky soils, which impart a distinct mineral edge to the wines grown here.

Wadandi Boodja Country Little Orenji – a stunning balanced Semillon / Sav Blanc. All organic fruit, hand harvested, fermented on skins for two weeks in open fermenters plus a giant cement egg for eight weeks pressed off to barrel & egg for full malo. Simply racked, a touch of sulphur to ensure you have a great product with no bottle variation or oxidation & bottled. - Jo Perry, Dormilona

Dja Dja Wurrung and Taungurung Country Bendigo riesling seems skin fermentation from small scale winemaker Scott Cosgriff. He’s make some terrific, left of centre but quality wines. Waxy texture on top of juiciness and saline notes. It’s got that hazy apple juice feel, dashes of sweet spice, ginger, green almond going on. A little sweetness to the fruit profile through the finish, so too a chalkiness lightly applied. Textural and good drinking ensues. - WineFront.com.au

Whadjuk Noongar Country. We love Ryan O'Meara from Express Winemakers, so much so that for the past several years we've been collaborating on unique wines with him under our collaborative label S'Express - it's a place for added creativity and left of centre releases that tickle our mutual fancy. The 2025 has blessed us with a seductively perfumed and plush one-two punch of syrah and pinot noir that deserves a spot in your fridge.

With its fruity lightness, noble herbal note and typical local minerality, the Riesling 2020 seduces in an irresistible way. A wonderfully fresh composition that unfolds light green nuances and treats you with its delicate bouquet of fine fruit. A brilliant companion to seafood, vegetable and pasta or fine fruity desserts. On a production trip in the summer of 2020, our contact with Anette Closheim came about through the recommendation of the hosts during a repeated stay in the Quartier Linde. A vintner who produces modern premium wines from the Nahe region in her family's 150-year-old vineyar

The Rosé from Provence indulges in light salmon pink with fine nuances of apricots, raspberries and floral notes. Lively smoothness and mineral freshness reflect the harmonious, French character. An exquisite companion to cold Mediterranean starters, bouillabaisse or grilled fish! A successful partnership that resulted from a kind of online dating. We are more than happy about that, because the wine cooperative Les Quatre Tours is emblematic of its symbolic attachment to the Coteaux d'Aix-en-Provence region and formidable art of living! Driven by their manifested core values - cooperation, qua

wine: Kolonne Null Non Alcoholic Cuvee Blanc No.01 375ml
notes: We present our sparkling fresh Cuvée Blanc No.1 - A harmonious combination of yellow fruit of pear and mirabelle, rounded off with a touch of typical brioche notes. The elegant acidity is balanced by a creamy, fine bubbly texture. Excellent as an aperitif or as a companion to fine canapés, seafood, fresh desserts such as zabaglione and panna cotta with fruit. wine: Rough Rice x PEP Borscht + Black Pepper Fermented Seasoning
notes: 8+ year old borscht perennial (wild fermented organic beetroot, red cabbage, purple carrot, garlic, dill, tarragon) freeze dried to harness flavour, nutrition and the luminescent lilac 🤝 single origin black pepper rounded with black cumin and seasalt. These botanicals macerate in the alcohol for two lunar moons, a vermouth produced without any added sugar. - Vivant Selections, importer

The movie was a childhood favourite of Mosse boys, Joseph and Sylvestre. Pineau d'Aunis and cabernet franc combine for a bright red crunchy wine. It'll prep you for anything the world has to throw at us! Bangarang is a négoce cuvée, made each year to sit somewhere between a rosé and a light red. It is 70% Grolleau Noir and 30% Cabernet Franc, both of which are directly pressed, plus they added a few buckets of Merlot added to boost its colour. Magic of Juju is a négoce wine which changes its composition a little each year. This year it is all sourced from the same Loire grower. The 2024 vintage is a blend of 60% Chenin Blanc 20% Chardonnay and 20% Sauvignon Blanc, all from vines that are on average of 30 years old . After a slow press, it was fermented and aged for 8 months in barrels on fine lees for 50% of the Chenin Blanc and all of the other varieties. It is mainly Grolleau Gris, with a tiny amount of Muscat à Petits Grains from Domaine Caterole in Roussillon, both of which were macerated for a few days (separately) to help create its pink hue, and 10% Merlot, a grape the Mosses don't usually use, which was directly pressed. It is from the same grower they source their other Loire négoce grapes from and according to Joseph Mosse was too good not to take! This is not meant to be a serious wine but is utterly delicious. - Living Wine, Importer

An estate wine called after the named place from where the grapes come where a plot of Cabernet Franc and Grolleau Noir grow side-by-side. The soil in clay on schist and are approximately 25 years old. It is 50% Cabernet Franc and 50% Grolleau Noir. The grapes were destemmed and then macerated for a week prior to pressing then aging on their less for 10 months in a tronic oak tank. The Grolleau Noir was picked first and the Cabernet Franc added the next day. It was bottled in July 2024. In weight it sits somewhere between the Cabernet Franc cuvée and Bisou. The tannins are noticeable but fine

wine: CELLAR RELEASE // Cappellano Barolo Pie Franco 2003
notes: This wine is the absolute rarest of the rare to begin with, and we've had a single bottle of the 2003 vintage squirreled away in our cellar for a years now, just waiting to see the light of day. Now is that time, and this is a not-to-be missed opportunity for serious Barolo lovers to get their hands on a beautifully aged bottle of one of the worlds truly great reds. Often considered the Holy Grail of Barolo, Cappellano’s Pie Franco is definitely one for the collectors and nebbiolo fanboys. It’s arguably the most delicate wine in the Cappellano stable, but it’s a wine of breathtaking intensity.

Spanish mackerel is deboned and cooked in salt water and then left for a short time to dry slightly before being rehydrated with a rich tomato sauce. A hunk of bread and some good quality butter and you on to a winner.

We are so excited this Genepy has landed! Family owned and completely artisanal, herbs are picked in the month of August in Graian Alps between the Aosta Valley and Piedmont. They are then dried and infused in pure alcohol fora month before re-distilling half of the infusion. Fresh, herbaceous and and with hints of cinnamon, lemon and mint. The perfect digestive!

The one everyone wants. Giuseppe 'Beppe' Rinaldi, nicknamed il citrico, one of Piedmont’s most vaunted producers was known for his tireless adherence to tradition. He farmed organically and fermented with the indigenous yeasts found in the ancient tini passed on by his father and grandfather and without temperature control. Most importantly, he was defiant in ensuring his Barolos were produced the ancient way, as blends – not from single vineyards. Having passed away in 2018 his legacy is safely in the hands of his daughters, Marta and Carlotta. There are no refunds on this wine

Giovanni Canonica farms one-and-a-half hectares of vines in the Paiagallo vineyard on the hill above Barolo. He and his family run a small agriturismo, and Canonica makes his wine in the cellars below. Everything here is traditional, and it's the integrity of this process that creates wines of both great breadth and intricate delicacy. Only a tiny number of bottles are produced each year, most of which are cellar-door sales. There are no refunds on this wine

She makes each of these beautiful, custom cups by hand and fires them to stoneware level so that they can withstand any temperature. Use them to drink cold wine, mulled wine, for coffee, tea, or water. Store your toothbrushes, put some flowers in them, hold your pens and pencils. Make your home and your life a little prettier. N.B. each and every piece is one-of-a-kind, no two are exactly alike!

Juicy, red and blue berry fruited, wild herb and distinct sage notes, salt bush, granitic minerality and some earthy, savoury, hazelnut notes between it all. Chisel to tannin, lots of layers to flavour, an overlay of general game meat and brambles, chewy texture through the finish and a starburst of orangey freshness meshed in. Wild island red wine feel, and so damn pleasurable and expressive in that regard. - The Wine Front

Cynar (pronounced chinar) is a much loved Italian bitter liqueur, named for the artichokes (Cynara Scolymus) that are the main flavouring ingredients. Slightly medicinal on the nose and palate with herbal and citrus flavor finishing soft and bitter. Drink over ice or can replace Campari in your favourite classic cocktails.

It was said to contain more than 27 different herbs and spices including aloe, rhubarb, and saffron, sourced from four continents. Its thick, bitter flavour and spices, makes it something of an acquired taste. It is perfect for a post dinner digestif and idea as a pick-me-up. Serve it over ice, with coke or just drink it straight (keep in in your freezer for when you want to drink it straight!).

Fragrant of red berries, cherry cola, raspberry and Aperol with similar flavours to taste. It's so damn fresh this thing it feels absolutely new born with each sip. It refreshes, it zings, it zips. Kaurna Country Naranjito is always centered around verdelho, with the addition of viognier and occasional other varieties as required from year to year to provide added structure and complexity. Always a wine that punchedswell above it's weight as far as price point goes. Everything biodynamically farmed and wild fermented, with skin contact times on different parcels ranging from fourteen all the way up to 180 days!

Ngunnawal County. Fresh pear, spiced green apple with savoury mandarin peel texture. Moderate pressings included for added texture and tannin extract. Mostly stainless steel barrel fermentation with a small percentage fermented as whole berries.- Mada Wines

Nixta Licor de Elote is a Mexican corn liqueur made from a base of tender, ancestral cacahuazintle (kaka • wha • SINT • lay) maize, grown in the high valleys and foothills of the Nevado de Toluca volcano. Nixta is produced at the Destilería y Bodega Abasolo, where we honor the Mexican culture of corn and the ancestral craft of nixtamalization—a 4,000 year old Mesoamerican cooking technique that uncovers the deepest flavors and aromas of maize. Intense straw with golden highlights in colour with notes of of sweet corn perfectly balanced with toasted notes of roasted corn, vanilla and caramel. -

wine: Alice and Olivier de Moor Chablis 1er Cru Vau de Vay 2023
notes: One of two de Moor vineyards in premier cru climats, Vau de Vey is on the left bank of the River Serein. It is composed of Kimmeridgian marl and limestone, with a south and eastern exposure, meaning it mainly gets morning not afternoon sun. It makes it one of Chablis' cooler climats. For this vintage Vau de Vay was aged initially in demi-muids (600 litres) then after a year blended into a foudre where it aged another year. It is well-balanced and precise with minerality without excessive acidity. Unsurprisingly it will be even more interesting if it can enjoy more aging. - Living Wines, Import

Think Chè đậu đỏ (Vietnamese Red Bean Dessert), red bean mochi or chocolate and walnuts in liquid form. Try pairing with or drizzling directly on yogurt, panna cotta, vanilla ice cream.

If Bonastre sounds familiar, it’s because it is also where you’ll find Partida Creus. It’s here Emi relished in her role as grape grower and winemaker for a number of years and formed a passion and confidence to commit fully to her own project. Emi now farms her own parcels of parrellada and sumoll near to her home and works with one of the region’s staple growers, Sebastia, to source beautifully farmed organic fruit. Punt e Mes literally means "point and a half" in Piedmontese, this Italian vermouth is half way between rosso vermouth and the Campari: one ”point” of sweetness and half a point of bitterness. Use as substitute for rosso vermouth in cocktails it is also most enjoyable over ice with an orange twist.

A Campari switch out. But distinct. And from Bologna. Hazy coloured but vibrant orange-red. Exotic. Energetic. Superbly bitter and zingy, blood orange, peppery, almost Szechuan characters here, a whoosh of orange juice and mandarin. It's nuts! This thing is so next level, and so textural and so interesting and good. All in. - WineFront.com.au

Created by Parisian chemist Joseph Dubonnet as a malaria preventative for soldiers serving in North Africa. Red and white wine from the from Rousillon region of France is fortified and blende with local herbs and spices such as quinine, orange peel, coffee beans, cinnamon and camomile before being aged for a minimum of three years. Drink on ice with a slice of lemon or in a Negroni in replacement of sweet vermouth.

wine: Mal Bien Mexicano by Victor & Emanuel Ramos
notes: This Mexicano mezcal is made from Agave Americana. Victor Ramos and his son Emanuel are third- and fourth-generation mezcal makers in Miahuatlán, Oaxaca. In this region, “Mexicano” refers to this specific type of agave. The agave is cooked underground for six days using wood, then rested, crushed, and fermented in wooden tanks. It is distilled twice in copper stills. Mal Bien Mexicano is extraordinary smooth and displays light vegetal notes, sweet wine, pine, bell pepper, and light smoke.

Distilled from the heart of the dasylirion plant (commonly known as Desert Spoon or, in Spanish, S otol) and is product in a similar manor as mezcal. The Sotol is picked at 12-15 years and roasted in shallow pits before being hand milled and distilled in copper pots. Sotol Ono is smooth and earthy with citrus and notes of minarality with a long sweet fruit finish. Perfect sipping here. Sotol liquor is known as the state spirit of Chihuahua.

wine: Fiore San Biagio Vino Cotto 375ml NV
notes: Vino Cotto is a sweeter style of wine, where the initial must (grape juice) is heated and reduced, a.k.a cooked. Then fresh must (grape juice) is added to kick off fermentation. The vino cotto is typically aged in barrel for long periods of time and topped up using cooked must from other vintages. Fiore San Biagio is located in Controguerra, on the Colline Teramane, on the border between Abruzzo and Marche. An incredible Japanese craft Absinthe. Made by Tatsumi-san by hand as a one-man operation. The Tatsumi Distillery Absinthe is made with 8 botanicals. Wormwood is the main ingredient along with anise. The Wormwood is sourced from a grower in Yamagata prefecture. The Absinthe is distilled from two different Shochu bases, Sweet Potato Shochu & Chicory Shochu. Utilising the famous Kabutogama still the Absinthe from Tatsumi-san is all handmade in very small batches of less than 500 bottles only once a year. Sweet note from sweet potato Shochu with wormwood and anise. The palate has a milky sweetnes

Marionette works closely with local farmers and this magical puppy is made with some "extremely rare blue mandarins (ahem)" and boy are we going along for the ride with this story!!! A classic retro liqueur using their Orange Curacao as the base so you know it is going to pop and zing. Someone whip up a batch of Blue Lagoons.

Created in the 1830s as a medicinal tonic by Amedee Peychaud, Peychaud's Bitters is a staple in the arsenal for any serious cocktail bartender. Gentian based, Peychaud's is more floral and sweeter compered to Angostura Bitters, it is a key ingredient for a Sazerac cocktail.
Bright red fruits here, a truly unique taste of cranberry with a rich aroma that would work well in cocktails, mixed with soda or even just over ice.

wine: Dark Emu: Aboriginal Australia and the Birth of Agriculture – Bruce Pascoe
notes: Author, academic and historian Bruce Pascoe has written one of the world’s most significant books, Dark Emu, a detailing of Australian history through a truer lens. The book re-examines colonial and contemporary accounts of Aboriginal people in Australia with evidence and detailing of the historical agriculture, life and culture of Aboriginal Australia. This is a non-negotiable read to understand and appreciate the deep history of Australia’s sustainable agriculture and the historical and future potential of farming in Australia.

wine: Argala Figli dei Fiori Sambuco (Elderberry Liqueur)
notes: Argala... which means to be satisfied! In this local Piemontese dialect. Lush, dark, and delicately spiced, Argala Figli dei Fiori Sambuco is a rich Italian elderberry liqueur layered with ripe berry character, gentle herbal notes, and a smooth, velvety finish. We love this one in a Hugo Spritz, take us back to Italy!

First created in 1786, Carpano Antica Formula is a highly sought after red vermouth. One of the first vermouths to ever be made, it’s rich velvety texture delivers initially sweet flavours before a beautiful turn to orange marmalade and warm spice bitterness. Traditionally served straight and well chilled as an aperitif, with a splash of soda or in Manhattans, Negronis or Martinez (just to name a few). No respectable bar runs without it!

The smell of a roadside watermelon cart in the south of Italy, where you can buy by the slice in the hot sun. The hills are dry and fragrant herbs are simmering. It's summer time. Spiced rum, vodka, gin or wine spritzers. Versatile and refreshing. A sophisticated soda. - Pyewacket's

It's a spring garden party at it's elegant best. Champagne spritz or shortcake, whatever you're feeling it sweet, pink and floral. A perfect introduction to shrubs for kids or those with a fun-only palette. - Pyewacket's

Aquavit, meaning ' water of life' is a distilled spirit that is principally produced in Scandinavia. Norway has been producing LINIE Aquavit by the same recipe from 1821, distilling the clear spirit from potatoes though a pot still with a special blend of herbs and spices. 28 months matured in ex-port casks, amber in colour and silky on the tongue the palate displays caraway, vanilla, aniseed and dried fruits delightfully. Designed to be drunk neat at room temperature.
Needs no explanation or introduction. Add a few drops to the tipple of your choice for maximum refreshment.
